The <audio> element is part of the broader HTML5 media effort, alongside <video>, the Media Source Extensions (MSE), and the Encrypted Media Extensions (EME). Together, they replaced Flash and made rich media a first-class citizen of the web.

docs.title: The Basic Syntax of <audio>
docs.text:
<audio controls>
    <source src="audio.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
    <source src="audio.ogg" type="audio/ogg">
    <p>Your browser does not support the audio element.</p>
</audio>

docs.title: Simple Audio Player
docs.text:
<audio controls>
    <source src="podcast.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

docs.title: Audio with Multiple Formats
docs.text:
<audio controls>
    <source src="audio.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
    <source src="audio.ogg" type="audio/ogg">
    <source src="audio.wav" type="audio/wav">
    <p>Your browser does not support the audio element.</p>
</audio>

docs.title: Audio with Preload
docs.text:
<audio controls preload="metadata">
    <source src="podcast.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

Preload values:

  • none – don't preload (save bandwidth).
  • metadata – preload only metadata (duration, dimensions).
  • auto – let the browser decide (may preload the whole file).

docs.title: Audio with Autoplay and Loop
docs.text:
<audio controls autoplay loop>
    <source src="ambient.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

Note: Autoplay is blocked by most browsers unless the audio is muted or the user has interacted with the page.

docs.title: Muted Audio
docs.text:
<audio controls muted>
    <source src="audio.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

docs.title: Audio Without Controls
docs.text:
<audio id="bgMusic" loop>
    <source src="ambient.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

<button onclick="document.getElementById('bgMusic').play()">Play</button>
<button onclick="document.getElementById('bgMusic').pause()">Pause</button>

docs.title: Audio with <track> (Captions)
docs.text:
<audio controls>
    <source src="speech.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
    <track kind="captions" src="speech.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default>
    <track kind="subtitles" src="speech-es.vtt" srclang="es" label="Español">
</audio>

docs.title: Audio Inside a <figure>
docs.text:
<figure>
    <audio controls preload="metadata">
        <source src="episode-1.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
        <track kind="captions" src="episode-1.vtt" srclang="en" label="English">
        <p>Your browser does not support the audio element.</p>
    </audio>
    <figcaption>Episode 1: The History of the Web</figcaption>
</figure>

docs.title: Code Breakdown
docs.text: Attribute Purpose controls Show native playback controls autoplay Start playing automatically (often blocked) loop Restart when finished muted Start muted preload none, metadata, or auto src The audio URL (alternative to <source>) crossorigin CORS setting <source> Alternative audio sources <track> Captions, subtitles, descriptions

docs.title: The "Music Player" Analogy
docs.text:
Think of <audio> as a music player embedded in the page. It has:

  • Play/pause controls.
  • Volume control.
  • Seek bar.
  • Time display.
  • Download option.

The controls attribute enables the native UI; without it, you build your own with JavaScript.

docs.title: The "Loading a Song" Mental Model
docs.text:
Loading audio is like loading a song on a device:

  1. Preload – whether to fetch the audio upfront or on demand.
  2. Fetch – the browser downloads the audio bytes.
  3. Decode – the browser decodes the compressed audio.
  4. Play – the browser outputs sound to the speakers.

Each step is controllable via attributes and the JS API.

docs.title: The "Multiple Format" Mental Model
docs.text: Different browsers support different audio formats. The <source> elements are candidates — the browser picks the first format it can play. This is exactly the same pattern as <picture> for images and <video> for video.

docs.title: The "Autoplay is Hostile" Mental Model
docs.text:
Browsers deliberately block autoplay because it's hostile to users — unexpected sound is jarring, especially in public places. To autoplay, the audio must be:

  • Muted (muted), OR
  • Triggered by user interaction (a click, tap, or key press).

Rule: Never autoplay audio without user consent.

docs.title: The "Plugin-Free" Mental Model
docs.text:
Before HTML5, audio required a plugin. Now it's native. This is a huge win for:

  • Users – no plugin to install.
  • Developers – simpler API, better compatibility.
  • Security – no plugin vulnerabilities.
  • Mobile – native support on iOS and Android.
  • Accessibility – native controls are accessible.

docs.title: Concept 1: The <audio> Element
docs.text:
The <audio> element is the container for audio content. It can have:

  • src attribute (alternative to <source>).
  • <source> children (candidates).
  • <track> children (captions).
  • Fallback content (shown if audio isn't supported).

docs.title: Concept 2: The <source> Element
docs.text:
The <source> element provides a candidate audio source:

<source src="audio.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
Attribute Purpose src The audio URL type MIME type (e.g., audio/mpeg)

The browser evaluates sources in order and picks the first supported one.

docs.title: Concept 3: The <track> Element
docs.text:
The <track> element provides timed text tracks (captions, subtitles, descriptions):

<track kind="captions" src="captions.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default>
Attribute Purpose kind captions, subtitles, descriptions, chapters, metadata src The WebVTT file URL srclang Language of the track label User-visible label default Enable by default

docs.title: Concept 4: Audio Formats
docs.text:
Format MIME Type Extension Browser Support MP3 audio/mpeg .mp3 All modern browsers AAC audio/aac .m4a, .aac All modern browsers Ogg Vorbis audio/ogg .ogg, .oga Chrome, Firefox, Edge Opus audio/opus .opus Chrome, Firefox, Edge WAV audio/wav .wav All modern browsers FLAC audio/flac .flac Chrome, Firefox, Edge WebM audio/webm .webm Chrome, Firefox, Edge

Best practice: Provide MP3 for universal support, and Ogg Vorbis or Opus for open-source browsers.

docs.title: Concept 5: The controls Attribute
docs.text:
The controls boolean attribute shows the browser's native playback controls:

<audio controls>

Controls typically include:

  • Play/pause.
  • Seek bar.
  • Volume.
  • Time display.
  • Download.
  • Playback speed (some browsers).

docs.title: Concept 6: The autoplay Attribute
docs.text:
The autoplay boolean attribute tells the browser to start playing automatically:

<audio autoplay muted>

Important: Browsers block autoplay unless:

  • The audio is muted, OR
  • The user has interacted with the page.

Best practice: Never autoplay unmuted audio.

docs.title: Concept 7: The loop Attribute
docs.text:
The loop boolean attribute restarts the audio when it ends:

<audio loop>

docs.title: Concept 8: The muted Attribute
docs.text:
The muted boolean attribute starts the audio muted:

<audio muted>

docs.title: Concept 9: The preload Attribute
docs.text:
The preload attribute tells the browser how much to preload:

Value Behaviour none Don't preload metadata Preload metadata only (duration) auto Let the browser decide

Best practice: Use metadata for most cases — it loads the duration without wasting bandwidth.

docs.title: Concept 10: The crossorigin Attribute
docs.text:
The crossorigin attribute controls CORS for cross-origin audio:

<audio crossorigin="anonymous">

Use case: When the audio is used with Web Audio API or Canvas visualization.

docs.title: Concept 11: The JavaScript API
docs.text:
The <audio> element exposes a rich JavaScript API:

Property/Method Description play() Start playback (returns a Promise) pause() Pause playback currentTime Current playback position (seconds) duration Total duration (seconds) volume Volume (0.0 to 1.0) muted Mute state paused Whether paused ended Whether ended loop Loop state playbackRate Speed (1.0 = normal) src The audio URL load() Reload the audio canPlayType(type) Check if a format is supported

docs.title: Concept 12: Audio Events
docs.text: Event Fires When play Playback starts pause Playback pauses ended Playback ends timeupdate Current time changes loadedmetadata Metadata loaded loadeddata First frame loaded canplay Can start playing canplaythrough Can play without buffering volumechange Volume changes seeking Seeking starts seeked Seeking ends error An error occurs

docs.title: Concept 13: Accessibility
docs.text:
• Native controls are keyboard-accessible.
  • <track> provides captions.
  • Transcripts should be provided.
  • aria-label for custom players.
  • Keyboard shortcuts for custom controls.

docs.title: Concept 14: Format Fallback
docs.text:
The browser evaluates <source> elements in order:

<source src="audio.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
<source src="audio.ogg" type="audio/ogg">

If MP3 is supported, it plays. If not, Ogg is tried.

docs.title: Concept 15: Fallback Content
docs.text:
Content between <audio> tags is shown if the browser doesn't support audio:

<audio controls>
    <source src="audio.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
    <p>Your browser doesn't support audio. <a href="audio.mp3">Download</a>.</p>
</audio>

docs.title: Concept 16: canPlayType()
docs.text:
const audio = document.createElement('audio');
console.log(audio.canPlayType('audio/mpeg')); // "probably" or "maybe" or ""

Return values:

  • "probably" – likely supported.
  • "maybe" – might be supported.
  • "" – not supported.

docs.title: Concept 17: The HTMLAudioElement Interface
docs.text: The <audio> element is represented by HTMLAudioElement, which inherits from HTMLMediaElement.

docs.title: Concept 18: Audio Streaming
docs.text:
The <audio> element supports streaming audio via HTTP range requests. This allows:

  • Progressive download – plays while downloading.
  • Seeking – jump to any point.
  • Live streams – via MSE or HLS (with JS).

docs.title: Concept 19: Audio and the Web Audio API
docs.text:
For advanced audio processing (visualization, effects, synthesis), use the Web Audio API with an AudioContext:

const audioContext = new AudioContext();
const source = audioContext.createMediaElementSource(audioElement);
const analyser = audioContext.createAnalyser();
source.connect(analyser);
analyser.connect(audioContext.destination);

docs.title: Concept 20: Audio Visualization
docs.text:
You can visualize audio using the Web Audio API and <canvas>:

const analyser = audioContext.createAnalyser();
const dataArray = new Uint8Array(analyser.frequencyBinCount);
analyser.getByteFrequencyData(dataArray);
// Draw bars on a canvas

docs.title: Concept 21: Autoplay Policies
docs.text:
Modern browsers have strict autoplay policies:

  • Chrome: Allows autoplay if muted or if the user has interacted with the site.
  • Firefox: Similar policy.
  • Safari: Requires user gesture for unmuted autoplay.
  • Mobile: Even stricter.

Best practice: Never autoplay unmuted audio.

docs.title: Concept 22: Audio and Mobile
docs.text:
On mobile:

  • Audio does not autoplay without user interaction.
  • Audio plays through the device's speaker or headphones.
  • Background audio may pause when the screen locks.
  • Audio continues in the background if the browser allows.

docs.title: Concept 23: Audio and CORS
docs.text:
Cross-origin audio requires CORS headers if:

  • Used with Web Audio API.
  • Used with Canvas visualization.
  • Used with crossorigin attribute.

docs.title: Concept 24: Audio and Captions
docs.text:
For audio content with speech, provide captions or transcripts:

  • <track kind="captions"> – for WebVTT captions.
  • Text transcript – for full accessibility.

docs.title: Concept 25: Audio and SEO
docs.text:
• Search engines index audio metadata (title, description).
  • Provide meaningful titles and descriptions.
  • Use structured data (PodcastEpisode) for podcasts.

docs.title: Step-by-Step: Browser Processing <audio>
docs.text:
1.  The parser encounters an `<audio>` element.
    │
    ▼
2.  It creates a DOM node for the audio.
    │
    ▼
3.  It reads the `src` attribute (if present).
    │
    ▼
4.  It processes each `<source>` child:
    │   ├── Reads the `src` and `type`.
    │   └── Checks if the format is supported.
    │
    ▼
5.  It processes each `<track>` child:
    │   └── Loads the captions file.
    │
    ▼
6.  It processes fallback content:
    │   └── Shows it if `<audio>` isn't supported.
    │
    ▼
7.  It preloads the audio based on `preload`.
    │
    ▼
8.  It renders the controls (if `controls` is set).
    │
    ▼
9.  If `autoplay` and allowed, it starts playing.
    │
    ▼
10. The `loadstart` event fires.
    │
    ▼
11. The audio loads.
    │
    ▼
12. The `loadedmetadata` event fires (duration available).
    │
    ▼
13. The `canplay` event fires.
    │
    ▼
14. The user interacts (or autoplay starts).
    │
    ▼
15. The `play` event fires.
    │
    ▼
16. Audio plays.
    │
    ▼
17. `timeupdate` events fire continuously.
    │
    ▼
18. The `ended` event fires (or `loop` restarts).

docs.title: Format Selection Algorithm
docs.text:
1. For each <source> in order:
  2. Read type.
  3. Call canPlayType(type).
  4. If supported, use this source.
  5. If none is supported, the <audio> element shows fallback content.

docs.title: The play() Promise
docs.text:
audio.play()
    .then(() => console.log('Playing'))
    .catch(error => console.error('Failed:', error));

Note: play() returns a Promise that rejects if autoplay is blocked.

docs.title: Event Sequence
docs.text:
1. loadstart – loading begins.
  2. durationchange – duration known.
  3. loadedmetadata – metadata loaded.
  4. loadeddata – first frame loaded.
  5. canplay – can start playing.
  6. canplaythrough – can play without buffering.
  7. play – playback starts.
  8. playing – playback actually begins.
  9. timeupdate – current time updates.
  10. pause – playback paused.
  11. ended – playback ended.

docs.title: Accessibility Tree
docs.text:
The <audio> element is exposed as:

  • role: application or group (varies).
  • name: from aria-label, title, or fallback content.

Note: Screen readers may treat <audio> differently. Custom controls need role="slider", aria-label, etc.

docs.title: Default User Agent Styles
docs.text:
audio {
    display: inline;
}

audio:not([controls]) {
    display: none;
}

The default size is typically 300 × 54 pixels when controls are visible.

docs.title: The HTMLAudioElement Interface
docs.text: <audio> is represented by HTMLAudioElement, which inherits from HTMLMediaElement.

docs.title: The HTMLMediaElement Interface
docs.text: Property/Method Description src The media URL currentSrc The actual URL used currentTime Current position duration Total duration paused Whether paused ended Whether ended muted Mute state volume Volume (0.0 to 1.0) playbackRate Speed defaultPlaybackRate Default speed loop Loop state preload Preload setting autoplay Autoplay setting controls Controls visibility networkState Network state readyState Ready state buffered Buffered ranges seekable Seekable ranges played Played ranges error Error object play() Start playing pause() Pause load() Reload canPlayType(type) Check support fastSeek(time) Fast seek

docs.title: The HTMLSourceElement Interface
docs.text: Property Description src The src attribute type The type attribute media The media attribute

docs.title: The HTMLTrackElement Interface
docs.text: Property Description kind Track kind src Track URL srclang Language label Label default Default flag readyState Loading state track The TextTrack object

docs.title: The TextTrack Interface
docs.text:
Represents a text track (captions, subtitles, etc.):

Property Description kind Track kind label User-visible label language Language mode disabled, hidden, showing cues List of cues activeCues Currently active cues

docs.title: The Audio Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Fetch – the browser downloads the audio bytes.
  2. Demux – splits the container into streams.
  3. Decode – decodes the compressed audio.
  4. Output – sends samples to the audio hardware.

docs.title: Browser Support for Formats
docs.text:
Browser MP3 AAC Ogg Opus WAV FLAC Chrome ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Firefox ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Safari ✅ ✅ ❌ ❌ ✅ ❌ Edge ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅

Note: Safari doesn't support Ogg or Opus natively.

docs.title: CORS and Audio
docs.text:
• crossorigin="anonymous" – requests without credentials.
  • crossorigin="use-credentials" – requests with credentials.

docs.title: The currentSrc Property
docs.text:
After source selection, currentSrc contains the URL actually used.

audio.currentSrc; // "https://example.com/audio.mp3"

docs.title: The networkState Property
docs.text: Value Meaning NETWORK_EMPTY (0) Not initialized NETWORK_IDLE (1) Idle NETWORK_LOADING (2) Loading NETWORK_NO_SOURCE (3) No source found

docs.title: The readyState Property
docs.text: Value Meaning HAVE_NOTHING (0) No data HAVE_METADATA (1) Metadata loaded HAVE_CURRENT_DATA (2) Current frame loaded HAVE_FUTURE_DATA (3) Future data loaded HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA (4) Enough to play

docs.title: The Lifecycle of an Audio Element
docs.text:
1.  Author writes `<audio>` with `<source>`.
    │
    ▼
2.  File deployed.
    │
    ▼
3.  Browser parses HTML and creates the DOM node.
    │
    ▼
4.  Browser evaluates `<source>` elements.
    │
    ▼
5.  Browser selects the first supported source.
    │
    ▼
6.  Browser preloads based on `preload`:
    │   ├── `none` → no load
    │   ├── `metadata` → load metadata
    │   └── `auto` → load as needed
    │
    ▼
7.  Browser fetches the audio.
    │
    ▼
8.  Browser decodes the audio.
    │
    ▼
9.  `loadedmetadata` event fires.
    │
    ▼
10. `canplay` event fires.
    │
    ▼
11. User interacts (or autoplay).
    │
    ▼
12. `play` event fires.
    │
    ▼
13. Audio plays.
    │
    ▼
14. `timeupdate` events fire.
    │
    ▼
15. Audio ends or loops.
    │
    ▼
16. `ended` event fires.

docs.title: Dynamic Audio Creation
docs.text:
const audio = new Audio('audio.mp3');
audio.controls = true;
audio.preload = 'metadata';
document.body.appendChild(audio);

docs.title: The Audio() Constructor
docs.text:
const audio = new Audio();
audio.src = 'audio.mp3';
audio.play();

Note: The Audio() constructor is a shorthand for document.createElement('audio').

docs.title: Example 1: Simple Audio Player
docs.text:
<audio controls>
    <source src="podcast.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
    <p>Your browser does not support the audio element.</p>
</audio>

docs.title: Example 2: Multiple Format Fallback
docs.text:
<audio controls>
    <source src="audio.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
    <source src="audio.ogg" type="audio/ogg">
    <source src="audio.wav" type="audio/wav">
    <p>Your browser does not support the audio element.</p>
</audio>

docs.title: Example 3: Preload Metadata
docs.text:
<audio controls preload="metadata">
    <source src="podcast.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

docs.title: Example 4: Loop and Autoplay (Muted)
docs.text:
<audio controls autoplay loop muted>
    <source src="ambient.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

docs.title: Example 5: Custom Controls
docs.text:
<audio id="myAudio">
    <source src="audio.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

<button id="playBtn">Play</button>
<button id="pauseBtn">Pause</button>
<input type="range" id="seekBar" min="0" max="100" value="0">

<script>
    const audio = document.getElementById('myAudio');
    document.getElementById('playBtn').addEventListener('click', () => audio.play());
    document.getElementById('pauseBtn').addEventListener('click', () => audio.pause());

    const seekBar = document.getElementById('seekBar');
    audio.addEventListener('timeupdate', () => {
        seekBar.value = (audio.currentTime / audio.duration) * 100;
    });
    seekBar.addEventListener('input', () => {
        audio.currentTime = (seekBar.value / 100) * audio.duration;
    });
</script>

docs.title: Example 6: Playlist
docs.text:
<audio id="player" controls>
    <source src="track1.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

<ul id="playlist">
    <li data-src="track1.mp3">Track 1</li>
    <li data-src="track2.mp3">Track 2</li>
    <li data-src="track3.mp3">Track 3</li>
</ul>

<script>
    const player = document.getElementById('player');
    document.querySelectorAll('#playlist li').forEach(item => {
        item.addEventListener('click', () => {
            player.src = item.dataset.src;
            player.play();
        });
    });
</script>

docs.title: Example 7: Audio with Captions
docs.text:
<audio controls>
    <source src="speech.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
    <track kind="captions" src="speech.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default>
    <track kind="subtitles" src="speech-es.vtt" srclang="es" label="Español">
</audio>

docs.title: Example 8: Audio Inside a <figure>
docs.text:
<figure>
    <audio controls preload="metadata">
        <source src="episode-1.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
        <track kind="captions" src="episode-1.vtt" srclang="en" label="English">
        <p>Your browser does not support audio. <a href="episode-1.mp3">Download</a>.</p>
    </audio>
    <figcaption>Episode 1: The History of the Web</figcaption>
</figure>

docs.title: Example 9: Audio with Volume Control
docs.text:
<audio id="audio" controls>
    <source src="music.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

<label for="volume">Volume:</label>
<input type="range" id="volume" min="0" max="1" step="0.01" value="1">

<script>
    const audio = document.getElementById('audio');
    const volume = document.getElementById('volume');
    volume.addEventListener('input', () => {
        audio.volume = volume.value;
    });
</script>

docs.title: Example 10: Playback Rate Control
docs.text:
<audio id="audio" controls>
    <source src="podcast.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

<label for="rate">Speed:</label>
<select id="rate">
    <option value="0.5">0.5×</option>
    <option value="1" selected>1×</option>
    <option value="1.5">1.5×</option>
    <option value="2">2×</option>
</select>

<script>
    document.getElementById('rate').addEventListener('change', (e) => {
        document.getElementById('audio').playbackRate = parseFloat(e.target.value);
    });
</script>

docs.title: Example 11: Audio Visualization
docs.text:
<audio id="audio" controls>
    <source src="music.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>
<canvas id="visualizer" width="600" height="200"></canvas>

<script>
    const audio = document.getElementById('audio');
    const canvas = document.getElementById('visualizer');
    const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');

    audio.addEventListener('play', () => {
        const audioContext = new AudioContext();
        const source = audioContext.createMediaElementSource(audio);
        const analyser = audioContext.createAnalyser();
        source.connect(analyser);
        analyser.connect(audioContext.destination);
        analyser.fftSize = 256;
        const bufferLength = analyser.frequencyBinCount;
        const dataArray = new Uint8Array(bufferLength);

        function draw() {
            requestAnimationFrame(draw);
            analyser.getByteFrequencyData(dataArray);
            ctx.fillStyle = 'rgb(20, 20, 20)';
            ctx.fillRect(0, 0, canvas.width, canvas.height);
            const barWidth = canvas.width / bufferLength;
            for (let i = 0; i < bufferLength; i++) {
                const barHeight = dataArray[i];
                ctx.fillStyle = 'rgb(' + (barHeight + 100) + ', 50, 50)';
                ctx.fillRect(i * barWidth, canvas.height - barHeight, barWidth - 1, barHeight);
            }
        }
        draw();
    });
</script>

docs.title: Example 12: Audio with Progress Bar
docs.text:
<audio id="audio" controls>
    <source src="music.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

<progress id="progress" value="0" max="100"></progress>
<span id="time">0:00 / 0:00</span>

<script>
    const audio = document.getElementById('audio');
    const progress = document.getElementById('progress');
    const time = document.getElementById('time');

    function formatTime(seconds) {
        const m = Math.floor(seconds / 60);
        const s = Math.floor(seconds % 60);
        return `${m}:${s.toString().padStart(2, '0')}`;
    }

    audio.addEventListener('timeupdate', () => {
        progress.value = (audio.currentTime / audio.duration) * 100;
        time.textContent = `${formatTime(audio.currentTime)} / ${formatTime(audio.duration)}`;
    });
</script>

docs.title: Example 13: Audio with Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text:
<audio id="audio" controls>
    <source src="music.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

<script>
    document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
        const audio = document.getElementById('audio');
        if (e.code === 'Space') {
            e.preventDefault();
            audio.paused ? audio.play() : audio.pause();
        } else if (e.code === 'ArrowLeft') {
            audio.currentTime -= 5;
        } else if (e.code === 'ArrowRight') {
            audio.currentTime += 5;
        } else if (e.code === 'ArrowUp') {
            audio.volume = Math.min(1, audio.volume + 0.1);
        } else if (e.code === 'ArrowDown') {
            audio.volume = Math.max(0, audio.volume - 0.1);
        }
    });
</script>

docs.title: Example 14: Autoplay with User Consent
docs.text:
<button id="enableAudio">Enable Background Music</button>
<audio id="bgMusic" loop>
    <source src="ambient.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

<script>
    document.getElementById('enableAudio').addEventListener('click', () => {
        document.getElementById('bgMusic').play();
    });
</script>

docs.title: Example 15: Loading State
docs.text:
<audio id="audio" controls>
    <source src="large-audio.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>
<div id="status" role="status" aria-live="polite"></div>

<script>
    const audio = document.getElementById('audio');
    const status = document.getElementById('status');

    audio.addEventListener('loadstart', () => status.textContent = 'Loading...');
    audio.addEventListener('canplay', () => status.textContent = 'Ready to play');
    audio.addEventListener('playing', () => status.textContent = 'Playing');
    audio.addEventListener('pause', () => status.textContent = 'Paused');
    audio.addEventListener('ended', () => status.textContent = 'Finished');
    audio.addEventListener('error', () => status.textContent = 'Error loading audio');
</script>

docs.title: Example 16: Audio with Chapters
docs.text:
<audio id="audio" controls>
    <source src="podcast.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
    <track kind="chapters" src="chapters.vtt" srclang="en" default>
</audio>

docs.title: Example 17: Audio with Download Link
docs.text:
<audio controls>
    <source src="podcast.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
    <p>Your browser doesn't support audio. <a href="podcast.mp3" download>Download</a>.</p>
</audio>

docs.title: Example 18: Audio with Structured Data (Podcast)
docs.text:
<article itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/PodcastEpisode">
    <h2 itemprop="name">Episode 1: The History of the Web</h2>
    <p itemprop="description">In this episode, we explore the origins of the web.</p>
    <audio controls itemprop="associatedMedia" itemscope itemtype="https://schema.org/MediaObject">
        <source src="episode-1.mp3" type="audio/mpeg" itemprop="contentUrl">
        <meta itemprop="duration" content="PT45M">
        <meta itemprop="encodingFormat" content="audio/mpeg">
    </audio>
</article>

docs.title: Example 19: Audio with Play/Pause Toggle
docs.text:
<button id="toggleBtn" aria-label="Play">▶</button>
<audio id="audio">
    <source src="music.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

<script>
    const audio = document.getElementById('audio');
    const btn = document.getElementById('toggleBtn');
    btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
        if (audio.paused) {
            audio.play();
            btn.textContent = '⏸';
            btn.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Pause');
        } else {
            audio.pause();
            btn.textContent = '▶';
            btn.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Play');
        }
    });
</script>

docs.title: Example 20: Complete Accessible Audio Player
docs.text:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <title>Accessible Audio Player</title>
    <style>
        body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; max-width: 600px; margin: 2rem auto; padding: 0 1rem; }
        .player { background: #f8f9fa; padding: 1rem; border-radius: 8px; border: 1px solid #dee2e6; }
        .controls { display: flex; gap: 0.5rem; align-items: center; margin-top: 1rem; flex-wrap: wrap; }
        button { padding: 0.5rem 1rem; min-height: 44px; min-width: 44px; border: none; border-radius: 4px; background: #3498db; color: white; cursor: pointer; font-size: 1rem; }
        button:hover { background: #2980b9; }
        button:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2c3e50; outline-offset: 2px; }
        input[type="range"] { flex: 1; min-width: 150px; }
        .time { font-family: monospace; font-size: 0.875rem; color: #6c757d; }
        progress { width: 100%; height: 8px; }
    </style>
</head>
<body>
    <h1>Accessible Audio Player</h1>
    <div class="player">
        <audio id="audio" preload="metadata">
            <source src="podcast.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
            <p>Your browser doesn't support audio. <a href="podcast.mp3" download>Download the audio</a>.</p>
        </audio>

        <progress id="progress" value="0" max="100" aria-label="Playback progress"></progress>
        <div class="time" id="timeDisplay" aria-live="off">0:00 / 0:00</div>

        <div class="controls">
            <button id="playPauseBtn" aria-label="Play">▶ Play</button>
            <button id="backBtn" aria-label="Rewind 10 seconds">⏪ 10s</button>
            <button id="forwardBtn" aria-label="Forward 10 seconds">10s ⏩</button>
            <label for="volume">Volume:</label>
            <input type="range" id="volume" min="0" max="1" step="0.01" value="1" aria-label="Volume">
        </div>

        <div id="status" role="status" aria-live="polite" style="margin-top: 0.5rem; color: #6c757d;"></div>
    </div>

    <script>
        const audio = document.getElementById('audio');
        const playPauseBtn = document.getElementById('playPauseBtn');
        const backBtn = document.getElementById('backBtn');
        const forwardBtn = document.getElementById('forwardBtn');
        const volume = document.getElementById('volume');
        const progress = document.getElementById('progress');
        const timeDisplay = document.getElementById('timeDisplay');
        const status = document.getElementById('status');

        function formatTime(seconds) {
            if (isNaN(seconds)) return '0:00';
            const m = Math.floor(seconds / 60);
            const s = Math.floor(seconds % 60);
            return `${m}:${s.toString().padStart(2, '0')}`;
        }

        playPauseBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
            if (audio.paused) {
                audio.play();
            } else {
                audio.pause();
            }
        });

        audio.addEventListener('play', () => {
            playPauseBtn.textContent = '⏸ Pause';
            playPauseBtn.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Pause');
            status.textContent = 'Playing';
        });

        audio.addEventListener('pause', () => {
            playPauseBtn.textContent = '▶ Play';
            playPauseBtn.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Play');
            status.textContent = 'Paused';
        });

        audio.addEventListener('timeupdate', () => {
            progress.value = (audio.currentTime / audio.duration) * 100;
            timeDisplay.textContent = `${formatTime(audio.currentTime)} / ${formatTime(audio.duration)}`;
        });

        audio.addEventListener('ended', () => {
            status.textContent = 'Finished';
            playPauseBtn.textContent = '▶ Play';
        });

        audio.addEventListener('error', () => {
            status.textContent = 'Error loading audio.';
        });

        backBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
            audio.currentTime = Math.max(0, audio.currentTime - 10);
        });

        forwardBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
            audio.currentTime = Math.min(audio.duration, audio.currentTime + 10);
        });

        volume.addEventListener('input', () => {
            audio.volume = volume.value;
        });

        progress.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
            const rect = progress.getBoundingClientRect();
            const percent = (e.clientX - rect.left) / rect.width;
            audio.currentTime = percent * audio.duration;
        });
    </script>
</body>
</html>

docs.title: 10. Common Use Cases
docs.text: Use Case Example Podcasts Episode playback with captions Music streaming Playlists and albums Sound effects Games and UI feedback Voice notes Recordings and messages Ambient sounds Background music (muted autoplay) Audiobooks Chapter navigation Language learning Pronunciation samples Audio descriptions Accessibility for video Notification sounds Alerts and reminders Meditation apps Timer and ambient sounds Radio streams Live audio Audio books Chaptered playback

docs.title: 11. Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Always include controls – unless building custom controls.
  2. Provide multiple formats – MP3 and Ogg.
  3. Use preload="metadata" – for most cases.
  4. Never autoplay unmuted – it's hostile.
  5. Provide fallback content – for unsupported browsers.
  6. Provide captions/transcripts – for accessibility.
  7. Use <track> – for captions and chapters.
  8. Label custom controls – with aria-label.
  9. Support keyboard – Space to play/pause, arrows for seek.
  10. Show loading state – with loadstart, canplay.
  11. Handle errors – listen for error events.
  12. Use crossorigin – if using Web Audio API.
  13. Test on mobile – iOS and Android behave differently.
  14. Test with screen readers – ensure controls are announced.
  15. Compress audio – use appropriate bitrate.
  16. Use a CDN – for faster delivery.
  17. Consider HLS/DASH – for adaptive streaming.
  18. Provide transcripts – for SEO and accessibility.
  19. Use structured data – for podcast rich results.
  20. Document your audio strategy – in a style guide.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Autoplay Unmuted
docs.text:
<audio autoplay>
    <source src="music.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

Why it's wrong: Browsers block it; users hate it.

✅ Correct: 

<audio autoplay muted>
    <source src="music.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

Or trigger on user interaction.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: No controls
docs.text:
<audio>
    <source src="music.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

Why it's wrong: No way for users to play/pause.

✅ Correct: 

<audio controls>
    <source src="music.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Single Format
docs.text:
<audio controls src="audio.ogg">

Why it's wrong: Safari doesn't support Ogg.

✅ Correct: 

<audio controls>
    <source src="audio.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
    <source src="audio.ogg" type="audio/ogg">
</audio>

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: No Fallback Content
docs.text:
<audio controls>
    <source src="audio.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

Why it's wrong: Users with old browsers see nothing.

✅ Correct: 

<audio controls>
    <source src="audio.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
    <p>Your browser doesn't support audio. <a href="audio.mp3">Download</a>.</p>
</audio>

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: No Captions for Speech
docs.text:
<audio controls>
    <source src="speech.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

Why it's wrong: Deaf and hard-of-hearing users can't access the content.

✅ Correct: 

<audio controls>
    <source src="speech.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
    <track kind="captions" src="speech.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default>
</audio>

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: No preload
docs.text:
<audio controls>
    <source src="large.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

Why it's wrong: Browser may preload the entire file, wasting bandwidth.

✅ Correct: 

<audio controls preload="metadata">
    <source src="large.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Missing type
docs.text:
<audio controls>
    <source src="audio.mp3">
</audio>

Why it's wrong: Browser must download the file to determine the format.

✅ Correct: 

<audio controls>
    <source src="audio.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: No Keyboard Support for Custom Controls
docs.text:
<button onclick="audio.play()">Play</button>

Why it's wrong: Custom buttons need keyboard support; use native <button>.

✅ Correct: Use <button> — it's keyboard-accessible by default.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Using Audio for Navigation Sounds
docs.text:
<audio autoplay>
    <source src="click.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
</audio>

Why it's wrong: Unexpected sounds are hostile.

✅ Correct: Only play sounds in response to user action.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: No Error Handling
docs.text:
audio.play();

Why it's wrong: If the file is missing, the promise rejects silently.

✅ Correct: 

audio.play().catch(error => console.error('Playback failed:', error));

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: No aria-label on Custom Controls
docs.text:
<button id="play">▶</button>

Why it's wrong: Screen readers announce "▶" with no context.

✅ Correct: 

<button id="play" aria-label="Play">▶</button>

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Not Testing on iOS
docs.text:
<audio autoplay>

Why it's wrong: iOS blocks autoplay even when muted in some cases.

✅ Correct: Test and provide play buttons.

docs.title: 13. Performance Considerations
docs.text:
• File size – compress audio; use appropriate bitrate.
  • Format – MP3 is universal; Ogg is smaller.
  • Preload – metadata avoids downloading the entire file.
  • Streaming – HTTP range requests enable seeking.
  • CDN – for global delivery.
  • Caching – long cache lifetimes.
  • Bitrate – 128 kbps for music, 64 kbps for speech.
  • Sample rate – 44.1 kHz for music, 22.05 kHz for speech.
  • Lazy loading – don't load until needed.

docs.title: Performance Tips
docs.text:
1. Compress audio – use FFmpeg or Audacity.
  2. Use preload="metadata".
  3. Use a CDN.
  4. Cache aggressively.
  5. Consider HLS/DASH for long audio.
  6. Avoid autoplay.
  7. Monitor bandwidth.

docs.title: 14. Security Considerations
docs.text:
• CORS – use crossorigin when needed.
  • HTTPS – required for secure playback.
  • Content-Security-Policy – restrict media sources with media-src.
  • Autoplay abuse – avoid unexpected audio.
  • User privacy – audio may reveal user behavior.
  • Malicious files – validate audio files.

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use HTTPS – for all audio.
  2. Set media-src in CSP.
  3. Validate uploads – file type, size, content.
  4. Avoid autoplay.
  5. Use crossorigin – for Web Audio API.
  6. Sanitize metadata – EXIF and ID3 tags.

docs.title: 15. Debugging Tips
docs.text:
• DevTools Elements panel – inspect the <audio> element.
  • Network panel – verify the audio request and size.
  • Console – check for errors and events.
  • audio.currentSrc – see the chosen source.
  • audio.readyState – check readiness.
  • audio.networkState – check network state.
  • audio.error – inspect errors.
  • audio.canPlayType() – test format support.
  • Event listeners – log events.
  • Lighthouse – audits for media.
  • Accessibility Inspector – check the role and name.
  • Screen reader testing – ensure controls are announced.
  • Test on mobile – iOS and Android.

docs.title: 16. When to Use
docs.text:
• For podcasts.
  • For music.
  • For sound effects.
  • For voice recordings.
  • For ambient sounds (muted).
  • For audio descriptions.
  • For language learning.
  • For audiobooks.
  • For notification sounds.

docs.title: 17. When Not to Use
docs.text:
• For video – use <video>.
  • For background music without consent – don't autoplay.
  • For non-audio content – use appropriate elements.
  • For visual effects – use CSS.

docs.title: 18. Related Concepts
docs.text:
• <video> – video element.
  • <source> – candidate sources.
  • <track> – captions and subtitles.
  • controls – native controls.
  • autoplay – autoplay.
  • loop – loop.
  • muted – mute.
  • preload – preload.
  • WebVTT – captions format.
  • Web Audio API – advanced audio.
  • Media Source Extensions – streaming.
  • Encrypted Media Extensions – DRM.
  • HLS/DASH – adaptive streaming.
  • HTMLAudioElement – DOM interface.
  • HTMLMediaElement – shared interface.
  • TextTrack – captions interface.
  • Accessibility – captions, transcripts.

docs.title: 19. Did You Know?
docs.text:
• The <audio> element was introduced in HTML5 (drafted 2008, standardized 2014).

  • It replaced Adobe Flash and other plugins for audio playback.

  • iOS never supported Flash — this was a major driver for native audio.

  • The <audio> element cannot autoplay unmuted in most browsers.

  • The preload="metadata" value loads only the duration, not the entire file.

  • MP3 is universally supported; Ogg Vorbis and Opus are open alternatives.

  • Safari doesn't support Ogg Vorbis or Opus natively.

  • WebVTT is the standard format for captions and subtitles.

  • The <track> element supports captions, subtitles, descriptions, chapters, and metadata.

  • The Web Audio API allows advanced processing: visualization, effects, synthesis.

  • Media Source Extensions (MSE) enable adaptive streaming (HLS, DASH).

  • Encrypted Media Extensions (EME) enable DRM.

  • canPlayType() returns "probably", "maybe", or "".

  • The play() method returns a Promise (unlike pause()).

  • The play() Promise rejects if autoplay is blocked.

  • currentSrc tells you which source the browser chose.

  • readyState values: HAVE_NOTHING, HAVE_METADATA, HAVE_CURRENT_DATA, HAVE_FUTURE_DATA, HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA.

  • networkState values: NETWORK_EMPTY, NETWORK_IDLE, NETWORK_LOADING, NETWORK_NO_SOURCE.

  • The Audio() constructor creates audio elements programmatically.

  • Accessibility: native controls are keyboard-accessible; custom controls need aria-label.

  • Best practices: controls, multiple formats, preload="metadata", fallback content, captions.

  • Common mistakes: autoplay unmuted, no controls, single format, no captions, no type.

  • Following best practices for audio leads to accessible, performant, and pleasant experiences.

docs.title: 20. Summary
docs.text:
• The <audio> element embeds sound content natively in HTML.
  • It replaced Adobe Flash and other plugins for audio playback.
  • Attributes: controls, autoplay, loop, muted, preload, src, crossorigin.
  • Child elements: <source> (candidate sources), <track> (captions).
  • JavaScript API: play(), pause(), currentTime, duration, volume, playbackRate, muted, loop.
  • Events: play, pause, ended, timeupdate, loadedmetadata, canplay, volumechange, seeking, error.
  • Best practices: controls, multiple formats, preload="metadata", never autoplay unmuted, fallback content, captions.
  • Common mistakes include autoplay unmuted, no controls, single format, missing type, and no captions.
  • Audio is essential for podcasts, music, sound effects, voice notes, and ambient sounds on the modern web.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
The <video> element is an HTML element that embeds video content directly into a web page. It allows developers to play video files — movies, tutorials, video calls, animations, and more — natively in the browser, without requiring third-party plugins like Adobe Flash, QuickTime, or Silverlight. The element provides built-in playback controls, supports multiple video formats through child <source> elements, and exposes a rich JavaScript API for programmatic control.

The <video> element is a media element, alongside <audio>. It is embedded content and phrasing content. It can appear anywhere phrasing content is accepted — inside <p>, <figure>, <div>, <li>, <td>, and more. It is one of the most important additions of HTML5, eliminating the plugin dependency that plagued the early web and enabling video to become a first-class citizen of the web platform.

Example: 

<video controls width="640" height="360" poster="thumbnail.jpg">
    <source src="movie.mp4" type="video/mp4">
    <source src="movie.webm" type="video/webm">
    <track kind="subtitles" src="subtitles.vtt" srclang="en" label="English">
    <p>Your browser does not support the video element.</p>
</video>

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The <video> element serves several essential purposes:

  • Native video playback – no plugins required.
  • Multiple formats – fallback via <source> elements.
  • Playback controls – play, pause, volume, seek, fullscreen, picture-in-picture.
  • Programmatic control – play, pause, seek, volume via JavaScript.
  • Events – play, pause, ended, timeupdate, volumechange, etc.
  • Accessibility – captions, subtitles, descriptions, keyboard-accessible controls.
  • Streaming – supports streaming video (via HTTP range requests).
  • Adaptive streaming – via Media Source Extensions (MSE) and HLS/DASH.
  • Picture-in-Picture – native PiP support.
  • Fullscreen – native fullscreen support.

docs.title: Where It Fits
docs.text:
The <video> element is embedded content and phrasing content. It is a block-level element when display: block is applied, but by default it is inline. It can be styled with CSS and controlled with JavaScript. It is the primary delivery mechanism for video on the web, from short clips to feature-length films, from live streams to interactive experiences.

<figure>
    <video controls width="800" height="450" poster="poster.jpg" preload="metadata">
        <source src="tutorial.mp4" type="video/mp4">
        <source src="tutorial.webm" type="video/webm">
        <track kind="captions" src="tutorial-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default>
        <track kind="captions" src="tutorial-es.vtt" srclang="es" label="Español">
        <p>Your browser does not support the video element. <a href="tutorial.mp4">Download the video</a>.</p>
    </video>
    <figcaption>Tutorial: Getting Started with HTML</figcaption>
</figure>

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text:
Before HTML5, playing video on the web required plugins. The dominant plugin was Adobe Flash, but others included QuickTime, RealPlayer, Windows Media Player, and Silverlight. Each plugin:

  • Required a separate installation.
  • Had its own security vulnerabilities.
  • Was proprietary and platform-specific.
  • Was often buggy and resource-heavy.
  • Was inaccessible to assistive technologies.
  • Didn't work on mobile devices (notably, iOS never supported Flash).
  • Consumed excessive CPU and battery.

This created a fragmented, fragile, and insecure ecosystem. Developers had to encode video in multiple formats for multiple plugins, and users had to install and maintain them. Video on the web was a second-class experience compared to native apps.

docs.title: Previous Limitations
docs.text: Limitation Consequence Plugin dependency Users had to install Flash/QuickTime Security vulnerabilities Flash was a constant attack target Platform-specific Not available on all devices (iOS) Inaccessible Screen readers couldn't access plugins Battery drain Flash consumed excessive CPU No standardization Each plugin had its own API No mobile support Flash never worked on iOS No native API Developers couldn't control playback easily No fullscreen/PiP Limited playback experience No adaptive streaming Same video for all connections

docs.title: Why the <video> Element Was Introduced
docs.text:
The <video> element was introduced in HTML5 (drafted in 2008, standardized in 2014) as part of the effort to eliminate plugin dependency. It was designed to:

  • Provide native video – no plugin required.
  • Support multiple formats – with <source> fallbacks.
  • Expose a JavaScript API – play, pause, seek, volume.
  • Fire events – for synchronization with other content.
  • Be accessible – native controls are keyboard-accessible; captions via <track>.
  • Work on mobile – iOS and Android support <video> natively.
  • Support captions – via <track> (WebVTT).
  • Be standardized – W3C/WHATWG specification.
  • Enable adaptive streaming – via MSE (Media Source Extensions).
  • Enable DRM – via EME (Encrypted Media Extensions).

The <video> element is part of the broader HTML5 media effort, alongside <audio>, MSE, and EME. Together, they replaced Flash and made rich media a first-class citizen of the web.

docs.title: The Basic Syntax of <video>
docs.text:
<video controls width="640" height="360">
    <source src="movie.mp4" type="video/mp4">
    <source src="movie.webm" type="video/webm">
    <p>Your browser does not support the video element.</p>
</video>

docs.title: Simple Video Player
docs.text:
<video controls width="640" height="360">
    <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

docs.title: Video with Multiple Formats
docs.text:
<video controls width="640" height="360">
    <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
    <source src="video.webm" type="video/webm">
    <source src="video.ogg" type="video/ogg">
    <p>Your browser does not support the video element.</p>
</video>

docs.title: Video with Poster Image
docs.text:
<video controls width="640" height="360" poster="thumbnail.jpg">
    <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

docs.title: Video with Preload
docs.text:
<video controls preload="metadata" width="640" height="360">
    <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

Preload values:

  • none – don't preload.
  • metadata – preload only metadata (duration, dimensions).
  • auto – let the browser decide.

docs.title: Video with Autoplay and Loop
docs.text:
<video controls autoplay loop muted width="640" height="360">
    <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

Note: Autoplay is blocked by most browsers unless the video is muted or the user has interacted with the page.

docs.title: Video with Captions
docs.text:
<video controls width="640" height="360">
    <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
    <track kind="captions" src="captions-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default>
    <track kind="subtitles" src="subtitles-es.vtt" srclang="es" label="Español">
    <track kind="descriptions" src="descriptions-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="Audio Description">
</video>

docs.title: Video with Poster and Fallback
docs.text:
<video controls width="640" height="360" poster="poster.jpg">
    <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
    <source src="video.webm" type="video/webm">
    <track kind="captions" src="captions.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default>
    <p>Your browser doesn't support video. <a href="video.mp4">Download the video</a>.</p>
</video>

docs.title: Video Inside a <figure>
docs.text:
<figure>
    <video controls width="800" height="450" poster="poster.jpg" preload="metadata">
        <source src="tutorial.mp4" type="video/mp4">
        <source src="tutorial.webm" type="video/webm">
        <track kind="captions" src="tutorial-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default>
        <p>Your browser doesn't support video. <a href="tutorial.mp4">Download</a>.</p>
    </video>
    <figcaption>Tutorial: Getting Started with HTML</figcaption>
</figure>

docs.title: Video with All Attributes
docs.text:
<video
    controls
    width="640"
    height="360"
    poster="poster.jpg"
    preload="metadata"
    playsinline
    crossorigin="anonymous"
    loop
    muted
    >
    <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
    <source src="video.webm" type="video/webm">
    <track kind="captions" src="captions.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default>
    <p>Your browser doesn't support the video element.</p>
</video>

docs.title: Code Breakdown
docs.text: Attribute Purpose controls Show native playback controls autoplay Start playing automatically (often blocked) loop Restart when finished muted Start muted preload none, metadata, or auto poster Thumbnail image before playback width / height Dimensions src The video URL (alternative to <source>) playsinline Prevent fullscreen on iOS crossorigin CORS setting <source> Alternative video sources <track> Captions, subtitles, descriptions, chapters

docs.title: The "Movie Theater" Analogy
docs.text:
Think of <video> as a movie theater embedded in the page. It has:

  • The screen – the video itself.
  • The stage – the <video> element.
  • The control booth – the JavaScript API.
  • The audience – the user.
  • The program – the video file.

The controls attribute opens the control booth to the user; without it, you build your own.

docs.title: The "Loading a Movie" Mental Model
docs.text:
Loading video is like loading a movie on a streaming service:

  1. Poster – the thumbnail before playback.
  2. Preload – whether to fetch the video upfront or on demand.
  3. Fetch – the browser downloads the video bytes.
  4. Decode – the browser decodes the compressed video.
  5. Render – the browser paints frames to the screen.
  6. Play – the browser outputs audio and video.

Each step is controllable via attributes and the JS API.

docs.title: The "Multiple Format" Mental Model
docs.text: Different browsers support different video formats. The <source> elements are candidates — the browser picks the first format it can play. This is exactly the same pattern as <picture> for images and <audio> for audio.

docs.title: The "Autoplay is Hostile" Mental Model
docs.text:
Browsers deliberately block autoplay because it's hostile to users — unexpected video (especially with sound) is jarring and wastes data. To autoplay, the video must be:

  • Muted (muted), OR
  • Triggered by user interaction (a click, tap, or key press).

Rule: Never autoplay unmuted video without user consent.

docs.title: The "Plugin-Free" Mental Model
docs.text:
Before HTML5, video required a plugin. Now it's native. This is a huge win for:

  • Users – no plugin to install.
  • Developers – simpler API, better compatibility.
  • Security – no plugin vulnerabilities.
  • Mobile – native support on iOS and Android.
  • Accessibility – native controls are accessible.

docs.title: The "Adaptive Streaming" Mental Model
docs.text:
Modern video delivery isn't just a single file — it's an adaptive stream that adjusts quality based on network conditions. This is achieved via:

  • MSE (Media Source Extensions) – allows JavaScript to feed video segments.
  • HLS (HTTP Live Streaming) – Apple's adaptive streaming protocol.
  • DASH (Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP) – open standard.
  • HLS.js and dash.js – JavaScript libraries for browsers without native support.

The <video> element is the player; MSE/HLS/DASH are the delivery mechanisms.

docs.title: Concept 1: The <video> Element
docs.text:
The <video> element is the container for video content. It can have:

  • src attribute (alternative to <source>).
  • <source> children (candidates).
  • <track> children (captions).
  • Fallback content (shown if video isn't supported).

docs.title: Concept 2: The <source> Element
docs.text:
The <source> element provides a candidate video source:

<source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
Attribute Purpose src The video URL type MIME type (e.g., video/mp4)

The browser evaluates sources in order and picks the first supported one.

docs.title: Concept 3: The <track> Element
docs.text:
The <track> element provides timed text tracks (captions, subtitles, descriptions, chapters):

<track kind="captions" src="captions.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default>
Attribute Purpose kind captions, subtitles, descriptions, chapters, metadata src The WebVTT file URL srclang Language of the track label User-visible label default Enable by default

docs.title: Concept 4: Video Formats
docs.text:
Format MIME Type Extension Browser Support MP4 (H.264) video/mp4 .mp4 All modern browsers WebM (VP8/VP9) video/webm .webm Chrome, Firefox, Edge Ogg (Theora) video/ogg .ogv Chrome, Firefox, Edge MOV (H.264) video/mp4 .mov Safari, Chrome AV1 video/mp4 .mp4 Chrome, Firefox, Edge HEVC/H.265 video/mp4 .mp4 Safari, Edge

Best practice: Provide MP4 (H.264) for universal support, and WebM (VP9) for open-source browsers.

docs.title: Concept 5: The controls Attribute
docs.text:
The controls boolean attribute shows the browser's native playback controls:

<video controls>

Controls typically include:

  • Play/pause.
  • Seek bar.
  • Volume.
  • Time display.
  • Fullscreen.
  • Picture-in-Picture.
  • Playback speed.
  • Captions/subtitles.

docs.title: Concept 6: The autoplay Attribute
docs.text:
The autoplay boolean attribute tells the browser to start playing automatically:

<video autoplay muted playsinline>

Important: Browsers block autoplay unless:

  • The video is muted, OR
  • The user has interacted with the page.

Best practice: Never autoplay unmuted video.

docs.title: Concept 7: The loop Attribute
docs.text:
The loop boolean attribute restarts the video when it ends:

<video loop>

docs.title: Concept 8: The muted Attribute
docs.text:
The muted boolean attribute starts the video muted:

<video muted>

docs.title: Concept 9: The preload Attribute
docs.text:
The preload attribute tells the browser how much to preload:

Value Behaviour none Don't preload metadata Preload metadata only (duration, dimensions) auto Let the browser decide

Best practice: Use metadata for most cases.

docs.title: Concept 10: The poster Attribute
docs.text:
The poster attribute specifies a thumbnail image shown before playback:

<video poster="thumbnail.jpg">

Why: Improves visual experience; shows content before the video loads.

docs.title: Concept 11: The width and height Attributes
docs.text:
Set the video dimensions:

<video width="640" height="360">

Why: Prevents layout shift (CLS) while the video loads.

docs.title: Concept 12: The playsinline Attribute
docs.text:
The playsinline attribute tells iOS Safari to play the video inline (not fullscreen):

<video playsinline>

Why: On iOS, videos autoplay fullscreen by default. playsinline keeps them in place.

docs.title: Concept 13: The crossorigin Attribute
docs.text:
The crossorigin attribute controls CORS for cross-origin video:

<video crossorigin="anonymous">

Use case: When the video is used with Canvas or Web Audio API.

docs.title: Concept 14: The JavaScript API
docs.text:
The <video> element exposes a rich JavaScript API:

Property/Method Description play() Start playback (returns a Promise) pause() Pause playback currentTime Current playback position (seconds) duration Total duration (seconds) volume Volume (0.0 to 1.0) muted Mute state paused Whether paused ended Whether ended loop Loop state playbackRate Speed (1.0 = normal) videoWidth Intrinsic video width videoHeight Intrinsic video height poster Poster URL src The video URL load() Reload the video canPlayType(type) Check if a format is supported requestFullscreen() Enter fullscreen requestPictureInPicture() Enter PiP textTracks Captions/subtitles

docs.title: Concept 15: Video Events
docs.text: Event Fires When play Playback starts pause Playback pauses ended Playback ends timeupdate Current time changes loadedmetadata Metadata loaded loadeddata First frame loaded canplay Can start playing canplaythrough Can play without buffering volumechange Volume changes seeking Seeking starts seeked Seeking ends waiting Waiting for data progress Downloading error An error occurs fullscreenchange Fullscreen toggled enterpictureinpicture PiP entered

docs.title: Concept 16: Captions and Subtitles
docs.text:
The <track> element provides captions and subtitles:

  • Captions – for deaf and hard-of-hearing users (includes sound effects).
  • Subtitles – for translation of dialogue.
  • Descriptions – audio descriptions for blind users.
  • Chapters – navigation markers.
  • Metadata – machine-readable data.

docs.title: Concept 17: WebVTT Format
docs.text:
Captions are stored in WebVTT (Web Video Text Tracks) format:

WEBVTT

00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:05.000
Hello, world!

00:00:05.000 --> 00:00:10.000
This is a caption.

docs.title: Concept 18: Accessibility
docs.text:
• Native controls are keyboard-accessible.
  • <track> provides captions.
  • Transcripts should be provided.
  • aria-label for custom players.
  • Keyboard shortcuts for custom controls.

docs.title: Concept 19: Format Fallback
docs.text:
The browser evaluates <source> elements in order:

<source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
<source src="video.webm" type="video/webm">

If MP4 is supported, it plays. If not, WebM is tried.

docs.title: Concept 20: Adaptive Streaming
docs.text:
• HLS – Apple's protocol; .m3u8 playlist.
  • DASH – open standard; .mpd manifest.
  • MSE – Media Source Extensions; JS API for feeding segments.
  • HLS.js – polyfill for browsers without native HLS.

docs.title: Concept 21: Picture-in-Picture
docs.text:
video.requestPictureInPicture();

Native PiP allows the video to float over other content.

docs.title: Concept 22: Fullscreen
docs.text:
video.requestFullscreen();

Native fullscreen expands the video.

docs.title: Concept 23: Video and CORS
docs.text:
Cross-origin video requires CORS headers if:

  • Used with Canvas or Web Audio API.
  • Used with crossorigin attribute.

docs.title: Concept 24: Video and Mobile
docs.text:
On mobile:

  • Video does not autoplay without user interaction (or must be muted).
  • playsinline keeps video inline on iOS.
  • Video may pause when the screen locks.
  • Video may continue in the background if the browser allows.

docs.title: Concept 25: Video and SEO
docs.text:
• Search engines index video metadata (title, description).
  • Provide meaningful titles and descriptions.
  • Use structured data (VideoObject) for rich results.

docs.title: Step-by-Step: Browser Processing <video>
docs.text:
1.  The parser encounters a `<video>` element.
    │
    ▼
2.  It creates a DOM node for the video.
    │
    ▼
3.  It reads the `src` attribute (if present).
    │
    ▼
4.  It processes each `<source>` child:
    │   ├── Reads the `src` and `type`.
    │   └── Checks if the format is supported.
    │
    ▼
5.  It processes each `<track>` child:
    │   └── Loads the captions file.
    │
    ▼
6.  It processes fallback content:
    │   └── Shows it if `<video>` isn't supported.
    │
    ▼
7.  It preloads the video based on `preload`.
    │
    ▼
8.  It displays the poster image (if set).
    │
    ▼
9.  It renders the controls (if `controls` is set).
    │
    ▼
10. If `autoplay` and allowed, it starts playing.
    │
    ▼
11. The `loadstart` event fires.
    │
    ▼
12. The video loads.
    │
    ▼
13. The `loadedmetadata` event fires (duration, dimensions).
    │
    ▼
14. The `loadeddata` event fires (first frame).
    │
    ▼
15. The `canplay` event fires.
    │
    ▼
16. The user interacts (or autoplay starts).
    │
    ▼
17. The `play` event fires.
    │
    ▼
18. Video plays.
    │
    ▼
19. `timeupdate` events fire continuously.
    │
    ▼
20. The `ended` event fires (or `loop` restarts).

docs.title: Format Selection Algorithm
docs.text:
1. For each <source> in order:
  2. Read type.
  3. Call canPlayType(type).
  4. If supported, use this source.
  5. If none is supported, the <video> element shows fallback content.

docs.title: The play() Promise
docs.text:
video.play()
    .then(() => console.log('Playing'))
    .catch(error => console.error('Failed:', error));

Note: play() returns a Promise that rejects if autoplay is blocked.

docs.title: Event Sequence
docs.text:
1. loadstart – loading begins.
  2. durationchange – duration known.
  3. loadedmetadata – metadata loaded.
  4. loadeddata – first frame loaded.
  5. canplay – can start playing.
  6. canplaythrough – can play without buffering.
  7. play – playback starts.
  8. playing – playback actually begins.
  9. timeupdate – current time updates.
  10. pause – playback paused.
  11. ended – playback ended.

docs.title: Accessibility Tree
docs.text:
The <video> element is exposed as:

  • role: application or group (varies).
  • name: from aria-label, title, or fallback content.

Note: Screen readers may treat <video> differently. Captions are essential.

docs.title: Default User Agent Styles
docs.text:
video {
    display: inline;
}

video:not([controls]) {
    display: none;
}

The default size is typically 300 × 150 pixels when controls are visible.

docs.title: The HTMLVideoElement Interface
docs.text: <video> is represented by HTMLVideoElement, which inherits from HTMLMediaElement.

docs.title: The HTMLMediaElement Interface
docs.text: Property/Method Description src The media URL currentSrc The actual URL used currentTime Current position duration Total duration paused Whether paused ended Whether ended muted Mute state volume Volume (0.0 to 1.0) playbackRate Speed loop Loop state preload Preload setting autoplay Autoplay setting controls Controls visibility networkState Network state readyState Ready state buffered Buffered ranges seekable Seekable ranges played Played ranges error Error object play() Start playing pause() Pause load() Reload canPlayType(type) Check support fastSeek(time) Fast seek

docs.title: The HTMLVideoElement Interface
docs.text:
HTMLVideoElement adds:

Property/Method Description width Display width height Display height videoWidth Intrinsic video width videoHeight Intrinsic video height poster Poster URL playsInline Plays inline flag requestPictureInPicture() Enter PiP disablePictureInPicture Disable PiP requestVideoFrameCallback(cb) Callback on new frame

docs.title: The HTMLSourceElement Interface
docs.text: Property Description src The src attribute type The type attribute media The media attribute

docs.title: The HTMLTrackElement Interface
docs.text: Property Description kind Track kind src Track URL srclang Language label Label default Default flag readyState Loading state track The TextTrack object

docs.title: The TextTrack Interface
docs.text:
Represents a text track (captions, subtitles, etc.):

Property Description kind Track kind label User-visible label language Language mode disabled, hidden, showing cues List of cues activeCues Currently active cues

docs.title: The Video Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Fetch – the browser downloads the video bytes.
  2. Demux – splits the container into streams.
  3. Decode – decodes the compressed video (and audio).
  4. Render – paints frames to the screen.
  5. Output – sends audio samples to the audio hardware.

docs.title: Browser Support for Formats
docs.text:
Browser MP4 (H.264) WebM (VP9) Ogg (Theora) AV1 Chrome ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Firefox ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Safari ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ (limited) Edge ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅

Note: Safari only supports MP4 (H.264) and HEVC.

docs.title: CORS and Video
docs.text:
• crossorigin="anonymous" – requests without credentials.
  • crossorigin="use-credentials" – requests with credentials.

docs.title: The currentSrc Property
docs.text:
After source selection, currentSrc contains the URL actually used.

video.currentSrc; // "https://example.com/video.mp4"

docs.title: The networkState Property
docs.text: Value Meaning NETWORK_EMPTY (0) Not initialized NETWORK_IDLE (1) Idle NETWORK_LOADING (2) Loading NETWORK_NO_SOURCE (3) No source found

docs.title: The readyState Property
docs.text: Value Meaning HAVE_NOTHING (0) No data HAVE_METADATA (1) Metadata loaded HAVE_CURRENT_DATA (2) Current frame loaded HAVE_FUTURE_DATA (3) Future data loaded HAVE_ENOUGH_DATA (4) Enough to play

docs.title: Media Source Extensions (MSE)
docs.text:
MSE allows JavaScript to feed video segments to the <video> element:

const mediaSource = new MediaSource();
video.src = URL.createObjectURL(mediaSource);
mediaSource.addEventListener('sourceopen', () => {
    const sourceBuffer = mediaSource.addSourceBuffer('video/mp4; codecs="avc1.42E01E"');
    sourceBuffer.appendBuffer(segment);
});

docs.title: Encrypted Media Extensions (EME)
docs.text:
EME enables DRM-protected content:

const access = await navigator.requestMediaKeySystemAccess('com.widevine.alpha', config);
const keys = await access.createMediaKeys();
await video.setMediaKeys(keys);

docs.title: The Lifecycle of a Video Element
docs.text:
1.  Author writes `<video>` with `<source>` and `<track>`.
    │
    ▼
2.  File deployed.
    │
    ▼
3.  Browser parses HTML and creates the DOM node.
    │
    ▼
4.  Browser evaluates `<source>` elements.
    │
    ▼
5.  Browser selects the first supported source.
    │
    ▼
6.  Browser displays the poster (if set).
    │
    ▼
7.  Browser preloads based on `preload`:
    │   ├── `none` → no load
    │   ├── `metadata` → load metadata
    │   └── `auto` → load as needed
    │
    ▼
8.  Browser fetches the video.
    │
    ▼
9.  Browser demuxes and decodes.
    │
    ▼
10. `loadedmetadata` event fires.
    │
    ▼
11. `loadeddata` event fires.
    │
    ▼
12. `canplay` event fires.
    │
    ▼
13. User interacts (or autoplay).
    │
    ▼
14. `play` event fires.
    │
    ▼
15. Video plays.
    │
    ▼
16. `timeupdate` events fire.
    │
    ▼
17. Video ends or loops.
    │
    ▼
18. `ended` event fires.

docs.title: Dynamic Video Creation
docs.text:
const video = document.createElement('video');
video.src = 'video.mp4';
video.controls = true;
video.preload = 'metadata';
document.body.appendChild(video);

docs.title: Example 8: Video with Custom Controls
docs.text:
<video id="video" width="640" height="360" poster="poster.jpg">
    <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

<button id="playBtn">Play</button>
<button id="pauseBtn">Pause</button>
<input type="range" id="seekBar" min="0" max="100" value="0">
<label for="volume">Volume:</label>
<input type="range" id="volume" min="0" max="1" step="0.01" value="1">

<script>
    const video = document.getElementById('video');
    document.getElementById('playBtn').addEventListener('click', () => video.play());
    document.getElementById('pauseBtn').addEventListener('click', () => video.pause());

    const seekBar = document.getElementById('seekBar');
    video.addEventListener('timeupdate', () => {
        seekBar.value = (video.currentTime / video.duration) * 100;
    });
    seekBar.addEventListener('input', () => {
        video.currentTime = (seekBar.value / 100) * video.duration;
    });

    const volume = document.getElementById('volume');
    volume.addEventListener('input', () => {
        video.volume = volume.value;
    });
</script>

docs.title: Example 9: Video with Playback Rate Control

<video id="video" controls width="640" height="360">
    <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

<label for="rate">Speed:</label>
<select id="rate">
    <option value="0.5">0.5×</option>
    <option value="1" selected>1×</option>
    <option value="1.5">1.5×</option>
    <option value="2">2×</option>
</select>

<script>

        document.getElementById('video').playbackRate = parseFloat(e.target.value);

</script>

docs.title: Example 10: Video with Fullscreen Button

    <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>
<button id="fsBtn">Fullscreen</button>

<script>
    document.getElementById('fsBtn').addEventListener('click', () => {
        const video = document.getElementById('video');
        if (document.fullscreenElement) {
            document.exitFullscreen();
        } else {
            video.requestFullscreen();
        }
    });
</script>

docs.title: Example 11: Video with Picture-in-Picture

</video>
<button id="pipBtn">Picture-in-Picture</button>

<script>
    document.getElementById('pipBtn').addEventListener('click', async () => {
        const video = document.getElementById('video');
        if (document.pictureInPictureElement) {
            await document.exitPictureInPicture();
        } else {
            await video.requestPictureInPicture();
        }
    });
</script>

docs.title: Example 12: Video with Loading State
docs.text:
<video id="video" controls width="640" height="360" poster="poster.jpg">
    <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>
<div id="status" role="status" aria-live="polite"></div>

<script>
    const video = document.getElementById('video');
    const status = document.getElementById('status');

    video.addEventListener('loadstart', () => status.textContent = 'Loading...');
    video.addEventListener('canplay', () => status.textContent = 'Ready to play');
    video.addEventListener('playing', () => status.textContent = 'Playing');
    video.addEventListener('pause', () => status.textContent = 'Paused');
    video.addEventListener('ended', () => status.textContent = 'Finished');
    video.addEventListener('error', () => status.textContent = 'Error loading video');
</script>

docs.title: Example 13: Video with Progress Bar
docs.text:
<video id="video" controls width="640" height="360">
    <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>
<progress id="progress" value="0" max="100"></progress>
<span id="time">0:00 / 0:00</span>

<script>
    const video = document.getElementById('video');
    const progress = document.getElementById('progress');
    const time = document.getElementById('time');

    function formatTime(seconds) {
        const m = Math.floor(seconds / 60);
        const s = Math.floor(seconds % 60);
        return `${m}:${s.toString().padStart(2, '0')}`;
    }

    video.addEventListener('timeupdate', () => {
        progress.value = (video.currentTime / video.duration) * 100;
        time.textContent = `${formatTime(video.currentTime)} / ${formatTime(video.duration)}`;
    });
</script>

docs.title: Example 16: Video with Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text:
<video id="video" controls width="640" height="360">
    <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

<script>
    document.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
        const video = document.getElementById('video');
        if (e.code === 'Space') {
            e.preventDefault();
            video.paused ? video.play() : video.pause();
        } else if (e.code === 'ArrowLeft') {
            video.currentTime -= 5;
        } else if (e.code === 'ArrowRight') {
            video.currentTime += 5;
        } else if (e.code === 'ArrowUp') {
            video.volume = Math.min(1, video.volume + 0.1);
        } else if (e.code === 'ArrowDown') {
            video.volume = Math.max(0, video.volume - 0.1);
        } else if (e.code === 'KeyF') {
            document.fullscreenElement ? document.exitFullscreen() : video.requestFullscreen();
        }
    });
</script>
