<style>
    .blur-up {
        filter: blur(10px);
        transition: filter 0.3s;
    }
    .blur-up.loaded {
        filter: blur(0);
    }
</style>

<script>
    const observer = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {
        entries.forEach(entry => {
            if (entry.isIntersecting) {
                const img = entry.target;

                newImg.src = img.dataset.src;
                newImg.onload = () => {

                    img.classList.add('loaded');

<script>

                script.src = 'https://example.com/chat-widget.js';

docs.title: Example 14: Lazy Loading Fallback for Older Browsers
docs.text:
<img data-src="photo.jpg" alt="Photo" class="lazy" width="800" height="600">
<noscript>
    <img src="photo.jpg" alt="Photo" width="800" height="600">
</noscript>

<script>
    // Feature detection
    if ('loading' in HTMLImageElement.prototype) {
        // Native lazy loading
        document.querySelectorAll('img[data-src]').forEach(img => {
            img.src = img.dataset.src;
            img.loading = 'lazy';
        });
    } else {
        // Fallback to Intersection Observer
        const observer = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {
            entries.forEach(entry => {
                if (entry.isIntersecting) {
                    const img = entry.target;
                    img.src = img.dataset.src;
                    observer.unobserve(img);
                }
            });
        });
        document.querySelectorAll('img[data-src]').forEach(img => observer.observe(img));
    }
</script>

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>

    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>Lazy Loading Demo</title>

        body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; max-width: 800px; margin: 2rem auto; padding: 0 1rem; }
        section { margin: 2rem 0; }

    <h1>Lazy Loading Demo</h1>

    <!-- LCP image: eager + high priority -->

    </section>

    <!-- Below-the-fold images: lazy -->

docs.title: 10. Common Use Cases
docs.text: Use Case Technique Below-the-fold images loading="lazy" Gallery images loading="lazy" Product images loading="lazy" Avatars loading="lazy" Ads loading="lazy" or Intersection Observer Embeds (YouTube, maps) loading="lazy" on iframe Social widgets Intersection Observer Background images Intersection Observer Videos preload="none" Third-party scripts Intersection Observer Chat widgets Intersection Observer Comments Intersection Observer Analytics Delayed loading Long pages content-visibility: auto

docs.title: 11. Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Lazy load below-the-fold images.
  2. Do NOT lazy load above-the-fold images.
  3. Use loading="lazy" for images and iframes.
  4. Use preload="none" for videos.
  5. Use Intersection Observer for other resources.
  6. Always set width and height – prevent CLS.
  7. Provide <noscript> fallbacks – for JS-based lazy loading.
  8. Use fetchpriority="high" for LCP images.
  9. Use rootMargin – load before the viewport.
  10. Test with DevTools – Network and Coverage panels.
  11. Test on slow connections – throttle in DevTools.
  12. Test on mobile – real devices.
  13. Monitor Core Web Vitals – LCP, CLS, INP.
  14. Don't lazy load critical content.
  15. Provide placeholders – for better UX.
  16. Consider blur-up – for visual continuity.
  17. Use content-visibility – for off-screen sections.
  18. Test in multiple browsers – Safari support varies.
  19. Consider feature detection – for older browsers.
  20. Document your lazy loading strategy – in a style guide.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Lazy Loading Above-the-Fold Images
docs.text:
<img src="hero.jpg" alt="Hero" loading="lazy">

Why it's wrong: Delays LCP; hurts performance.

✅ Correct: 

<img src="hero.jpg" alt="Hero" fetchpriority="high">

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: No width/height
docs.text:
<img src="photo.jpg" alt="Photo" loading="lazy">

Why it's wrong: Causes layout shift (CLS).

✅ Correct: 

<img src="photo.jpg" alt="Photo" loading="lazy" width="800" height="600">

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: No <noscript> Fallback
docs.text:
<img data-src="photo.jpg" alt="Photo" class="lazy">

Why it's wrong: Users with JS disabled see nothing.

✅ Correct: 

<img data-src="photo.jpg" alt="Photo" class="lazy">
<noscript>
    <img src="photo.jpg" alt="Photo">
</noscript>

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Lazy Loading the LCP Image
docs.text:
<img src="hero.jpg" alt="Hero" loading="lazy">

Why it's wrong: LCP is the most important metric; lazy loading delays it.

✅ Correct: Use fetchpriority="high" and no loading="lazy".

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Not Testing on Slow Connections
docs.text:
Why it's wrong: Lazy loading is most important on slow connections.

✅ Correct: Use DevTools network throttling.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Using loading="lazy" on <video>
docs.text:
<video loading="lazy">

Why it's wrong: <video> doesn't support loading.

✅ Correct: 

<video preload="none">

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Not Unobserving Elements
docs.text:
const observer = new IntersectionObserver((entries) => {
    entries.forEach(entry => {
        if (entry.isIntersecting) {
            const img = entry.target;
            img.src = img.dataset.src;
            // Missing: observer.unobserve(img);
        }
    });
});

Why it's wrong: Wastes resources re-checking.

✅ Correct: 

observer.unobserve(entry.target);

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: No Placeholder
docs.text:
<img data-src="photo.jpg" alt="Photo" class="lazy">

Why it's wrong: Users see a blank space.

✅ Correct: Use a placeholder or skeleton.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: No alt on Lazy Images
docs.text:
<img data-src="photo.jpg" class="lazy">

Why it's wrong: Accessibility failure.

✅ Correct: 

<img data-src="photo.jpg" alt="A scenic view" class="lazy">

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Lazy Loading Everything
docs.text:
<img src="logo.png" alt="Logo" loading="lazy">

Why it's wrong: Above-the-fold content should load eagerly.

✅ Correct: 

<img src="logo.png" alt="Logo">

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Not Testing on Safari
docs.text:
Why it's wrong: Safari's support varies by version.

✅ Correct: Test on Safari 15.4+ (images) and 16.4+ (iframes).

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: No Feature Detection
docs.text:
Why it's wrong: Older browsers won't lazy load.

✅ Correct: Feature-detect and fall back.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Lazy Loading Ads Without Fallback
docs.text:
Why it's wrong: Ads might not load; revenue lost.

✅ Correct: Provide a fallback for ad blockers.

docs.title: 13. Performance Considerations
docs.text:
• Initial load – reduced significantly.
  • Bandwidth – saved for off-screen content.
  • Core Web Vitals – improves LCP, CLS, INP.
  • Server load – fewer requests.
  • Battery – less CPU and network.
  • Cache – lazy-loaded images cache normally.
  • HTTP/2 – reduces request overhead but lazy loading still saves bandwidth.
  • Placeholders – add minimal cost.
  • Intersection Observer – efficient; no scroll listeners.

docs.title: Performance Tips
docs.text:
1. Use native lazy loading – faster than JS.
  2. Set dimensions – prevent CLS.
  3. Use fetchpriority – for priorities.
  4. Preload LCP images – for LCP.
  5. Use content-visibility – for off-screen sections.
  6. Minify HTML – reduce file size.
  7. Test with Lighthouse.

docs.title: 14. Security Considerations
docs.text:
• XSS – don't use user input in src or data-src without sanitization.
  • CORS – lazy-loaded cross-origin resources need CORS.
  • CSP – restrict resource sources with img-src, frame-src.
  • Placeholder – don't leak sensitive data.
  • Ad blockers – lazy-loaded ads may be blocked.
  • Tracking – lazy loading may affect analytics (content not loaded = no tracking).

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Sanitize user input – for src.
  2. Use HTTPS – for all resources.
  3. Set CSP – restrict resource sources.
  4. Validate URLs – for lazy-loaded resources.
  5. Test with ad blockers.

docs.title: 15. Debugging Tips
docs.text:
• DevTools Network panel – filter by image, scroll, see when images load.
  • Coverage panel – see unused bytes.
  • Lighthouse – audits for lazy loading.
  • Performance panel – inspect LCP and CLS.
  • img.loading – check the attribute.
  • img.currentSrc – see the loaded URL.
  • Intersection Observer – log entries.
  • Test with slow connections – DevTools throttling.
  • Test on mobile – real devices.
  • WebPageTest – filmstrip view.

docs.title: 16. When to Use
docs.text:
• For below-the-fold images.
  • For iframes below the fold.
  • For videos (preload="none").
  • For ads.
  • For social widgets.
  • For third-party scripts.
  • For long pages.
  • For galleries.
  • For mobile-heavy sites.

docs.title: 17. When Not to Use
docs.text:
• For above-the-fold images – LCP.
  • For critical content – must load immediately.
  • For small images – no benefit.
  • For SEO-critical images – index carefully.
  • For accessibility-critical content – may not load for screen readers.

docs.title: 18. Related Concepts
docs.text:
• loading attribute – native lazy loading.
  • preload attribute – video preload.
  • fetchpriority – priority hints.
  • Intersection Observer API – JS lazy loading.
  • rootMargin – loading distance.
  • threshold – visibility threshold.
  • content-visibility – CSS deferring.
  • srcset, sizes – responsive images.
  • preload, prefetch, preconnect – resource hints.
  • Core Web Vitals – LCP, CLS, INP.
  • Layout Shift (CLS) – visual stability.
  • Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) – main content timing.
  • Service Workers – offline/caching.
  • Lazy loading libraries – lazysizes, lozad.

docs.title: 19. Did You Know?
docs.text:
• Native lazy loading was introduced in Chrome 76 (2019).

  • Firefox followed in 75 (2020); Safari in 15.4 (2022).

  • The loading attribute is supported on <img> and <iframe>.

  • Browsers use heuristics to decide when to load lazy images.

  • Chrome loads lazy images within ~1250px on fast connections.

  • The Intersection Observer API was introduced in 2016.

  • rootMargin lets you load resources before they enter the viewport.

  • threshold defines how much of the element must be visible.

  • loading="lazy" is a progressive enhancement — older browsers load eagerly.

  • Lazy loading can hurt LCP if applied to the LCP element.

  • fetchpriority="high" is the correct tool for LCP images.

  • preload="none" on <video> defers video loading.

  • content-visibility: auto skips rendering off-screen content.

  • Lazy loading saves bandwidth, improves UX, and reduces battery drain.

  • Googlebot supports lazy loading and scrolls pages to trigger it.

  • Best practices: native loading, dimensions, placeholders, noscript fallback.

  • Common mistakes: lazy loading above-the-fold, no dimensions, no fallback.

  • Following best practices for lazy loading leads to faster, more efficient, and more accessible web pages.

docs.title: 20. Summary
docs.text:
• Lazy loading defers loading of non-critical resources until they're near the viewport.
  • Native support via loading="lazy" on <img> and <iframe>.
  • Videos use preload="none".
  • Other resources use the Intersection Observer API.
  • Best practices: lazy load below-the-fold, eager load above-the-fold, set dimensions, provide fallbacks, use fetchpriority.
  • Common mistakes: lazy loading LCP images, no dimensions, no <noscript>, no feature detection.
  • Lazy loading improves performance, bandwidth, battery life, and Core Web Vitals.
  • It is essential for modern, high-performance, mobile-friendly web pages.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
Media performance is the practice of optimising images, video, audio, and other embedded media so they load quickly, render smoothly, and consume minimal bandwidth, memory, and CPU — without sacrificing visual quality or user experience. It is the discipline of delivering rich media to every user, on every device, on every network condition, at the lowest reasonable cost.

Media is the heaviest part of the modern web. Images alone account for roughly 50% of a typical page's weight, and video can push a page past several megabytes. Optimising media is therefore the single highest-leverage performance improvement available to most websites.

Media performance combines:

  • Format selection – JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, SVG, MP4, WebM.
  • Compression – reducing file size without visible quality loss.
  • Responsive delivery – serving the right size to the right device.
  • Lazy loading – deferring off-screen media.
  • Resource hints – preload, preconnect, prefetch.
  • Caching and CDNs – global, cached delivery.
  • Layout stability – reserving space to prevent CLS.
  • Core Web Vitals – LCP, CLS, INP.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Media performance serves several essential purposes:

  • Speed – faster page loads; better user experience.
  • Bandwidth savings – lower data usage, especially on mobile.
  • Battery savings – less CPU and network activity.
  • SEO – Google uses page speed as a ranking factor.
  • Core Web Vitals – directly affected by media delivery.
  • Conversion – faster pages convert better.
  • Accessibility – faster media benefits users on slow connections.
  • Scalability – pages remain fast as media grows.
  • Cost savings – lower bandwidth and CDN costs.

docs.title: Where It Fits
docs.text:
Media performance is a cross-cutting concern spanning:

Media Performance
│
├── Images (formats, compression, srcset, lazy loading)
├── Video (codecs, streaming, poster, preload)
├── Audio (compression, preload)
├── SVG (optimisation)
├── Resource Hints (preload, preconnect, prefetch)
├── Layout Stability (width/height, aspect-ratio)
├── Caching (HTTP cache, CDN, Service Workers)
└── Core Web Vitals (LCP, CLS, INP)

It touches every layer of the stack: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, server configuration, and infrastructure.

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text:
The modern web is media-heavy. A typical page loads:

  • Dozens of images – hero, thumbnails, avatars, icons, backgrounds.
  • Multiple videos – autoplay loops, embedded players, ads.
  • Audio files – podcasts, sound effects.
  • Fonts and icons – often vector but still network requests.

Without optimisation, this media:

  • Delays the first paint – the browser waits for large images.
  • Increases LCP – the largest element takes longer to appear.
  • Causes layout shift – images without dimensions push content around.
  • Wastes bandwidth – serving 4000px images to 400px phones.
  • Drains battery – decoding large media is CPU-intensive.
  • Slows interactivity – the main thread is busy decoding.
  • Hurts SEO – Google penalises slow pages.
  • Reduces conversions – every 100ms of delay costs revenue.

A single unoptimised hero image can add several seconds to a page load. Multiply that across a catalogue of thousands of pages, and the impact is enormous.

docs.title: Previous Limitations
docs.text: Limitation Consequence One image for all devices Wasted bandwidth or blurry images JPEG/PNG only Larger files than modern formats No lazy loading All images loaded upfront No responsive images Same size for all viewports No format fallback Couldn't use modern formats No layout reservation Layout shift (CLS) No caching strategy Repeated downloads No CDN Slow global delivery No compression Bloated files No resource hints Late discovery of critical media

docs.title: Why Media Performance Became Critical
docs.text:
Three trends made media performance essential:

  1. Mobile dominance – over 60% of traffic is mobile; mobile networks are slower and data is metered.
  2. Core Web Vitals – Google made LCP, CLS, and INP ranking signals in 2021.
  3. Rich media expectations – users expect high-quality images and video, but not at the cost of speed.

Media performance is now a first-class engineering discipline, not an afterthought.

docs.title: Image Performance Checklist
docs.text: Technique Implementation Modern format AVIF, WebP with fallbacks Responsive images srcset + sizes Dimensions width and height Lazy loading loading="lazy" Priority hint fetchpriority="high" for LCP Decoding decoding="async" Preload <link rel="preload"> for LCP Compression Squoosh, ImageOptim, SVGO

docs.text:
<img src="photo-800.jpg"
     srcset="photo-400.jpg 400w,
             photo-800.jpg 800w,

     alt="A scenic mountain view"

<link rel="preload"
      as="image"
      href="hero-1200.jpg"
      imagesrcset="hero-600.jpg 600w, hero-1200.jpg 1200w"
      imagesizes="100vw">

<img src="hero-1200.jpg"

     sizes="100vw"

docs.text:
<picture>
    <source srcset="image.avif" type="image/avif">
    <source srcset="image.webp" type="image/webp">
    <img src="image.jpg" alt="A photo" width="800" height="600">
</picture>

docs.text:
<video controls preload="none" poster="poster.jpg" playsinline width="640" height="360">
    <source src="video.webm" type="video/webm">
    <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

docs.title: Resource Hints
docs.text:
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://cdn.example.com">
<link rel="dns-prefetch" href="https://cdn.example.com">
<link rel="preload" as="font" href="font.woff2" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
<link rel="prefetch" href="next-page.html">

docs.title: Code Breakdown
docs.text: Technique Purpose srcset + sizes Serve the right size loading="lazy" Defer off-screen media fetchpriority="high" Prioritise LCP decoding="async" Decode off the main thread <picture> Art direction + format fallback preload Fetch critical media early preconnect Establish early connections preload="none" Defer video poster Show image before video plays width / height Prevent layout shift

docs.title: The "Weight Lifter" Analogy
docs.text: Think of the page as a weight lifter. Media is the weight. The lighter the media (smaller files), the easier it is for the browser (and network) to carry. Every kilobyte saved is a kilogram lifted off the page.

docs.title: The "Water Pipe" Analogy
docs.text: The network is a water pipe. Media is water. A narrow pipe (slow connection) can only carry so much at once. Sending less water (smaller files) means it arrives faster. Serving the right amount (responsive images) prevents overflow (wasted bandwidth).

docs.title: The "Delivery Truck" Analogy
docs.text: The browser is a delivery truck. Each media file is a parcel. Without optimisation, the truck tries to deliver thousands of parcels at once. With lazy loading, it delivers only what the customer needs, when they need it, at the right size.

docs.title: The "Concentric Priorities" Mental Model
docs.text:
Media has priorities, and performance is about matching them:

Priority 1 (Highest):  LCP image (hero)
Priority 2:            Above-the-fold media
Priority 3:            Below-the-fold media
Priority 4 (Lowest):   Off-screen, optional media
  • LCP image: preload, fetchpriority="high", eager.
  • Above-the-fold: eager, no lazy loading.
  • Below-the-fold: lazy loading.
  • Off-screen: lazy loading, deferred, content-visibility.

docs.title: The "Budget" Mental Model
docs.text:
Every page has a performance budget:

  • Weight budget – e.g., ≤ 1 MB total, ≤ 300 KB images.
  • Request budget – e.g., ≤ 50 requests.
  • LCP budget – e.g., ≤ 2.5 s on 4G.
  • CLS budget – e.g., ≤ 0.1.

Optimising media is about staying within budget.

docs.title: The "First Impression" Mental Model
docs.text: LCP is the first impression of the page. If the hero image loads slowly, users perceive the page as slow — even if everything else is fast. Prioritising the LCP image is the single most impactful optimisation.

docs.title: Concept 1: Core Web Vitals
docs.text:
Three metrics measure user experience:

Metric Meaning Target LCP (Largest Contentful Paint) When the largest element renders ≤ 2.5 s CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) Visual stability ≤ 0.1 INP (Interaction to Next Paint) Responsiveness ≤ 200 ms

Media impact:

  • LCP – usually an image or video poster.
  • CLS – caused by images without dimensions.
  • INP – affected by heavy decoding on the main thread.

docs.title: Concept 2: Image Formats
docs.text:
Format Best For Compression Browser Support JPEG Photos Good Universal PNG Graphics, transparency Poor Universal GIF Simple animations Very poor Universal WebP Modern all-purpose Excellent All modern AVIF Modern best compression Best Chrome, Firefox, Safari 16+ SVG Icons, vector N/A Universal

Best practice: Use AVIF with WebP fallback and JPEG/PNG as final fallback.

docs.title: Concept 3: Responsive Images
docs.text:
Serve the right size:

<img srcset="photo-400.jpg 400w, photo-800.jpg 800w, photo-1200.jpg 1200w"
     sizes="(max-width: 600px) 100vw, 50vw"
     src="photo-800.jpg" alt="A photo">

Impact: Reduces bandwidth by 50–80% on mobile.

docs.title: Concept 4: Lazy Loading
docs.text:
Defer off-screen media:

<img src="photo.jpg" alt="Photo" loading="lazy">

Impact: Reduces initial load by 30–60% on media-heavy pages.

docs.title: Concept 5: Layout Stability
docs.text:
Always set dimensions:

<img src="photo.jpg" alt="Photo" width="800" height="600">

Or with CSS:

img { aspect-ratio: 4 / 3; width: 100%; height: auto; }

Impact: Prevents CLS entirely.

docs.title: Concept 6: Compression
docs.text:
Reduce file size without visible quality loss:

  • JPEG: 70–85% quality.
  • WebP: 75–85% quality.
  • AVIF: 50–60% quality.
  • PNG: use pngquant or convert to WebP.
  • SVG: use SVGO.

Impact: Reduces file size by 30–70%.

docs.title: Concept 7: Modern Codecs for Video
docs.text:
Codec Container Compression Support H.264 MP4 Good Universal VP9 WebM Better Chrome, Firefox, Edge AV1 MP4/WebM Best Modern browsers

Best practice: Provide AV1/VP9 with H.264 fallback.

docs.title: Concept 8: Video Preload
docs.text:
<video controls preload="none" poster="poster.jpg">

Values:

  • none – don't preload (best for below-the-fold).
  • metadata – load metadata only.
  • auto – let the browser decide (avoid).

docs.title: Concept 9: Resource Hints
docs.text: Hint Purpose preconnect Establish early connection dns-prefetch Resolve DNS early preload Fetch critical resource early prefetch Fetch for future navigation prerender Render a future page

docs.title: Concept 10: Preload for LCP
docs.text:
<link rel="preload" as="image" href="hero.jpg" fetchpriority="high">

Impact: Reduces LCP by 200–800 ms.

docs.title: Concept 11: fetchpriority
docs.text: Value Use Case high LCP images low Below-the-fold images auto Default

docs.title: Concept 12: decoding="async"
docs.text:
<img src="photo.jpg" alt="Photo" decoding="async">

Impact: Decodes images off the main thread, improving INP.

docs.title: Concept 13: CDN for Media
docs.text:
• Global edge servers – reduce latency.
  • Automatic optimisation – WebP, AVIF, resizing.
  • Caching – reduce origin load.
  • Image resizing APIs – Cloudinary, Imgix, Cloudflare Images.

docs.title: Concept 14: Caching
docs.text:
• Cache-Control – long cache lifetimes for immutable assets.
  • ETag – conditional requests.
  • Service Workers – offline caching.

docs.title: Concept 15: content-visibility
docs.text:
.lazy-section {
    content-visibility: auto;
    contain-intrinsic-size: 500px;
}

Impact: Skips rendering off-screen sections, improving initial render.

docs.title: Concept 16: Font Performance
docs.text:
• Use font-display: swap – avoids invisible text.
  • Subset fonts – only needed characters.
  • Preload critical fonts – for above-the-fold text.
  • Use WOFF2 – best compression.

docs.title: Concept 17: SVG Performance
docs.text:
• Optimise with SVGO – remove metadata.
  • Inline critical SVG – avoid HTTP requests.
  • Use <symbol> + <use> – for icon sprites.

docs.title: Concept 18: Background Images
docs.text:
.hero {
    background-image: image-set(
        url('hero-1x.avif') type('image/avif') 1x,
        url('hero-2x.avif') type('image/avif') 2x,
        url('hero-1x.webp') type('image/webp') 1x,
        url('hero-2x.webp') type('image/webp') 2x
    );
}

Note: image-set() support varies.

docs.title: Concept 19: Media Performance Budgets
docs.text:
A typical budget:

Metric Budget Total page weight ≤ 1.5 MB Images ≤ 500 KB Video (poster) ≤ 100 KB LCP ≤ 2.5 s CLS ≤ 0.1 INP ≤ 200 ms

docs.title: Concept 20: Measuring Performance
docs.text: Tool Purpose Lighthouse Audits PageSpeed Insights Field + lab data WebPageTest Detailed waterfall Chrome DevTools Network, Performance, Coverage CrUX Real-user metrics

docs.title: Concept 21: Field vs. Lab Data
docs.text:
• Lab – synthetic tests (Lighthouse).
  • Field – real-user metrics (CrUX, RUM).

Both matter. Lab is reproducible; field reflects reality.

docs.title: Concept 22: Image CDNs
docs.text:
Services like Cloudinary, Imgix, and Cloudflare Images:

  • Resize on the fly.
  • Convert to modern formats.
  • Cache globally.
  • Optimise automatically.
<img src="https://cdn.example.com/image/upload/w_800,f_auto,q_auto/photo.jpg">

docs.title: Concept 23: Picture Element for Art Direction
docs.text:
<picture>
    <source media="(min-width: 1200px)" srcset="hero-wide.avif" type="image/avif">
    <source media="(min-width: 1200px)" srcset="hero-wide.jpg" type="image/jpeg">
    <img src="hero-small.jpg" alt="Hero" width="800" height="400">
</picture>

docs.title: Concept 24: Video Streaming
docs.text:
• HLS – Apple's adaptive streaming.
  • DASH – open adaptive streaming.
  • MSE – Media Source Extensions.

Impact: Quality adjusts to network; reduces buffering.

docs.title: Concept 25: Media and SEO
docs.text:
• Page speed – ranking factor.
  • Image SEO – alt text, filenames, structured data.
  • Video SEO – structured data (VideoObject), transcripts.

docs.title: Step-by-Step: Image Loading Pipeline
docs.text:
1.  Browser parses HTML.
    │
    ▼
2.  Encounters `<img>`.
    │
    ▼
3.  Evaluates `srcset` and `sizes`:
    │   └── Chooses the best candidate.
    │
    ▼
4.  Checks cache:
    │   ├── Hit → load from cache.
    │   └── Miss → fetch from network.
    │
    ▼
5.  Fetches the image (or from cache).
    │
    ▼
6.  Decodes the image:
    │   ├── `sync` → blocks main thread.
    │   └── `async` → decodes off thread.
    │
    ▼
7.  Paints the image.
    │
    ▼
8.  Records LCP (if this is the LCP element).

docs.title: Step-by-Step: Video Loading Pipeline
docs.text:
1.  Browser parses `<video>`.
    │
    ▼
2.  Reads `preload` and `poster`.
    │
    ▼
3.  If `preload="none"`:
    │   └── Only poster is displayed.
    │
    ▼
4.  User clicks play.
    │
    ▼
5.  Browser fetches video (or from cache).
    │
    ▼
6.  Demuxes and decodes.
    │
    ▼
7.  Renders frames.
    │
    ▼
8.  Outputs audio.

docs.title: The LCP Algorithm
docs.text:
The browser tracks the largest element rendered in the viewport:

  1. Starts at navigation.
  2. Ends at first user interaction or when the page is fully loaded.
  3. Records the largest paint (image, video poster, text block).
  4. LCP = time from navigation to that paint.

Optimising LCP:

  • Preload the LCP image.
  • Use fetchpriority="high".
  • Serve a modern format.
  • Serve the right size.
  • Avoid lazy loading.

docs.title: The CLS Algorithm
docs.text:
The browser tracks unexpected layout shifts:

  1. Each shift is scored by impact (size of shifted area) × distance.
  2. The score accumulates over the page's lifetime.
  3. CLS = the largest burst of shifts (windowed).

Optimising CLS:

  • Set width/height.
  • Use aspect-ratio.
  • Reserve space for ads.
  • Avoid inserting content above existing content.

docs.title: The INP Algorithm
docs.text:
INP measures interaction latency:

  1. From user input to the next paint.
  2. Includes processing time, presentation delay.
  3. INP = the worst interaction (or 98th percentile).

Optimising INP:

  • Reduce main-thread work.
  • Use decoding="async".
  • Use Web Workers.
  • Break long tasks.

docs.title: Browser Heuristics for Lazy Loading
docs.text:
• Chrome: loads lazy images within ~1250px (fast), ~2500px (slow).
  • Firefox: similar.
  • Safari: near viewport.

docs.title: Resource Hints Flow
docs.text:
preconnect → DNS + TCP + TLS → ready for requests
preload    → fetch critical resource early
prefetch   → fetch for future navigation (idle time)
dns-prefetch → DNS only (lighter than preconnect)

docs.title: CDN Flow
docs.text:
User → nearest edge → cached media → fast delivery
                  ↓ (cache miss)
              origin server → cache at edge

docs.title: The Browser Image Cache
docs.text:
Images are cached based on:

  • Cache-Control headers.
  • ETag / Last-Modified.
  • Expires.

Once cached, repeated views are instant.

docs.title: The HTMLImageElement Performance Properties
docs.text: Property Description naturalWidth Intrinsic width naturalHeight Intrinsic height currentSrc The chosen URL complete Loaded or not decode() Decode promise loading lazy or eager fetchPriority Priority hint decoding sync, async, auto

docs.title: The PerformanceObserver API
docs.text:
const observer = new PerformanceObserver((list) => {
    for (const entry of list.getEntries()) {
        console.log(entry.name, entry.startTime);
    }
});
observer.observe({ type: 'largest-contentful-paint', buffered: true });
observer.observe({ type: 'layout-shift', buffered: true });

docs.title: The PerformanceResourceTiming API
docs.text:
Provides timing for each resource:

const resources = performance.getEntriesByType('resource');
resources.forEach(r => {
    console.log(r.name, r.duration, r.transferSize);
});

docs.title: The Navigation Timing API
docs.text:
Provides page load timings:

const nav = performance.getEntriesByType('navigation')[0];
console.log(nav.domContentLoadedEventEnd);
console.log(nav.loadEventEnd);

docs.title: Image Decode and Paint
docs.text:
• Fetch – downloads bytes.
  • Decode – converts bytes to pixels.
  • Paint – draws pixels on screen.

decoding="async" defers decoding to off-thread, improving INP.

docs.title: Video Decode and Render
docs.text:
• Demux – splits container.
  • Decode – decodes video and audio.
  • Render – paints frames.
  • Output – plays audio.

Hardware decoding (H.264, HEVC) is more efficient than software.

docs.title: Resource Priorities
docs.text:
Chrome assigns priorities:

  • Highest: HTML, CSS, fonts, LCP images.
  • High: scripts, above-the-fold images.
  • Medium: below-the-fold images.
  • Low: prefetch, off-screen.

fetchpriority overrides these heuristics.

docs.title: Service Worker Caching
docs.text:
self.addEventListener('fetch', (event) => {
    event.respondWith(
        caches.match(event.request).then(r => r || fetch(event.request))
    );
});

Enables offline and fast repeat views.

docs.title: The Browser Memory Cache
docs.text: Small, short-lived cache for resources used in the current page. Not to be confused with the disk cache.

docs.title: The Lifecycle of Media Performance
docs.text:
1.  Author writes HTML with optimised media.
    │
    ▼
2.  Build tools optimise (compress, generate variants).
    │
    ▼
3.  Deploy to CDN.
    │
    ▼
4.  Browser fetches HTML.
    │
    ▼
5.  Browser parses and prioritises media.
    │
    ▼
6.  Browser loads critical media eagerly.
    │
    ▼
7.  Browser lazy loads below-the-fold.
    │
    ▼
8.  User scrolls; lazy media loads.
    │
    ▼
9.  Metrics recorded (LCP, CLS, INP).
    │
    ▼
10. RUM sends metrics to analytics.
    │
    ▼
11. Team monitors and improves.

docs.title: Continuous Improvement
docs.text:
Media performance is a cycle:

  1. Measure – Lighthouse, CrUX, RUM.
  2. Identify – largest media, worst offenders.
  3. Optimise – compress, resize, change format.
  4. Deploy – CDN, caching.
  5. Re-measure – verify improvement.
  6. Repeat.

docs.title: Example 1: Optimised Hero Image
docs.text:
<link rel="preload" as="image" href="hero-1200.jpg"
      imagesrcset="hero-600.jpg 600w, hero-1200.jpg 1200w"
      imagesizes="100vw">

<img src="hero-1200.jpg"
     srcset="hero-600.jpg 600w, hero-1200.jpg 1200w"
     sizes="100vw"
     alt="A panoramic mountain landscape"
     fetchpriority="high"
     width="1200" height="600">

docs.title: Example 2: Lazy-Loaded Gallery
docs.text:
<img src="photo-1-400.jpg"
     srcset="photo-1-400.jpg 400w, photo-1-800.jpg 800w"
     sizes="(max-width: 600px) 100vw, 300px"
     alt="Gallery image 1"
     loading="lazy"
     decoding="async"
     width="400" height="300">

docs.title: Example 3: Modern Format Fallback
docs.text:
<picture>
    <source srcset="image.avif" type="image/avif">
    <source srcset="image.webp" type="image/webp">
    <img src="image.jpg" alt="A photo" width="800" height="600" loading="lazy">
</picture>

docs.title: Example 4: Optimised Video
docs.text:
<video controls preload="none" poster="poster.webp" playsinline width="640" height="360">
    <source src="video.av1.mp4" type="video/mp4; codecs=av01.0.05M.08">
    <source src="video.vp9.webm" type="video/webm; codecs=vp9">
    <source src="video.h264.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

docs.title: Example 5: Resource Hints
docs.text:
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://cdn.example.com">
<link rel="dns-prefetch" href="https://analytics.example.com">
<link rel="preload" as="font" href="font.woff2" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
<link rel="preload" as="image" href="hero.jpg" fetchpriority="high">

docs.title: Example 6: Responsive Background Image
docs.text:
.hero {
    background-image: image-set(
        url('hero-1x.webp') type('image/webp') 1x,
        url('hero-2x.webp') type('image/webp') 2x
    );
    background-size: cover;
    background-position: center;

const observer = new PerformanceObserver((list) => {
    for (const entry of list.getEntries()) {
        console.log('LCP:', entry.startTime, entry.element);

});

docs.title: Example 12: PerformanceObserver for CLS
docs.text:
let cls = 0;
const observer = new PerformanceObserver((list) => {
    for (const entry of list.getEntries()) {
        if (!entry.hadRecentInput) {
            cls += entry.value;
        }
    }
    console.log('CLS:', cls);
});
observer.observe({ type: 'layout-shift', buffered: true });

docs.title: Example 19: Service Worker Cache
docs.text:
const CACHE = 'v1';
const ASSETS = ['/', '/styles.css', '/hero.webp'];
self.addEventListener('install', (event) => {
    event.waitUntil(caches.open(CACHE).then(c => c.addAll(ASSETS)));
});
self.addEventListener('fetch', (event) => {
    event.respondWith(
        caches.match(event.request).then(r => r || fetch(event.request))
    );
});

docs.title: Example 20: Complete Optimised Page
docs.text:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>Optimised Media Page</title>

    <!-- Resource Hints -->
    <link rel="preconnect" href="https://cdn.example.com" crossorigin>
    <link rel="dns-prefetch" href="https://cdn.example.com">

    <!-- Preload LCP image -->
    <link rel="preload" as="image" href="hero-1200.jpg"
          imagesrcset="hero-600.jpg 600w, hero-1200.jpg 1200w"
          imagesizes="100vw">

    <style>
        body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; max-width: 1200px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 0 1rem; }
        img { display: block; max-width: 100%; height: auto; }
        .hero { aspect-ratio: 2 / 1; object-fit: cover; border-radius: 8px; }
        .gallery { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(250px, 1fr)); gap: 1rem; list-style: none; padding: 0; }
        .gallery img { aspect-ratio: 4 / 3; object-fit: cover; border-radius: 8px; }
    </style>
</head>
<body>
    <h1>Optimised Media Page</h1>

    <!-- LCP: Eager, high priority -->
    <picture>
        <source srcset="hero-1200.avif 1200w, hero-600.avif 600w" type="image/avif" sizes="100vw">
        <source srcset="hero-1200.webp 1200w, hero-600.webp 600w" type="image/webp" sizes="100vw">
        <img src="hero-1200.jpg"
             srcset="hero-600.jpg 600w, hero-1200.jpg 1200w"
             sizes="100vw"
             alt="A panoramic mountain landscape at sunrise"
             class="hero"
             fetchpriority="high"
             width="1200" height="600">
    </picture>

    <!-- Gallery: Lazy, responsive -->
    <h2>Gallery</h2>
    <ul class="gallery">
        <li>
            <picture>
                <source srcset="photo-1-800.avif 800w" type="image/avif">
                <source srcset="photo-1-800.webp 800w" type="image/webp">
                <img src="photo-1-800.jpg"
                     srcset="photo-1-400.jpg 400w, photo-1-800.jpg 800w"
                     sizes="(max-width: 600px) 100vw, 250px"
                     alt="A mountain landscape"
                     loading="lazy"
                     decoding="async"
                     width="800" height="600">
            </picture>
        </li>
        <li>
            <picture>
                <source srcset="photo-2-800.avif 800w" type="image/avif">
                <source srcset="photo-2-800.webp 800w" type="image/webp">
                <img src="photo-2-800.jpg"
                     srcset="photo-2-400.jpg 400w, photo-2-800.jpg 800w"
                     sizes="(max-width: 600px) 100vw, 250px"
                     alt="A calm lake at dawn"
                     loading="lazy"
                     decoding="async"
                     width="800" height="600">
            </picture>
        </li>
    </ul>

    <!-- Video: Preload none -->
    <h2>Video</h2>
    <video controls preload="none" poster="poster.webp" playsinline width="640" height="360">
        <source src="video.webm" type="video/webm">
        <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
    </video>
</body>
</html>

docs.title: 10. Common Use Cases
docs.text: Use Case Optimisation E-commerce Responsive images, lazy loading, WebP/AVIF News sites LCP preload, lazy loading, image CDN Blogs Responsive images, lazy loading Galleries srcset + sizes, lazy loading Video streaming Adaptive streaming (HLS/DASH) Landing pages LCP preload, eager hero Dashboards Lazy loading, content-visibility Mobile apps (PWA) Service Worker caching Social media Lazy loading, responsive images Documentation Optimised SVG, preloaded fonts

docs.title: 11. Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use modern formats – AVIF, WebP.
  2. Provide fallbacks – JPEG, PNG.
  3. Use srcset + sizes – responsive images.
  4. Set width/height – prevent CLS.
  5. Lazy load below-the-fold – loading="lazy".
  6. Eager load above-the-fold – no lazy loading.
  7. Preload LCP image – <link rel="preload">.
  8. Use fetchpriority="high" – for LCP.
  9. Use decoding="async" – for non-critical images.
  10. Compress images – 70–85% quality.
  11. Use a CDN – global, cached delivery.
  12. Use preload="none" for videos – defer.
  13. Provide posters – for videos.
  14. Optimise SVG – with SVGO.
  15. Subset fonts – only needed characters.
  16. Preconnect to CDNs – early connections.
  17. Set Cache-Control – long cache lifetimes.
  18. Test with Lighthouse – regularly.
  19. Monitor Core Web Vitals – with RUM.
  20. Document your strategy – in a style guide.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Serving 4000px Images to 400px Phones
docs.text:
<img src="photo-4000.jpg" alt="Photo" width="400" height="300">

Why it's wrong: Wastes bandwidth, slows load.

✅ Correct: Use srcset.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: No Dimensions
docs.text:
<img src="photo.jpg" alt="Photo">

Why it's wrong: Causes CLS.

✅ Correct: Add width and height.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Lazy Loading LCP Image
docs.text:
<img src="hero.jpg" alt="Hero" loading="lazy">

Why it's wrong: Hurts LCP.

✅ Correct: fetchpriority="high", no lazy.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: No Preload for LCP
docs.text:
<img src="hero.jpg" alt="Hero" fetchpriority="high">

Why it's wrong: Browser discovers it late.

✅ Correct: Add <link rel="preload">.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Loading All Images Eagerly
docs.text:
<img src="photo-1.jpg" alt="Photo 1">
<img src="photo-2.jpg" alt="Photo 2">
<!-- 50 more -->

Why it's wrong: Slow initial load.

✅ Correct: Add loading="lazy".

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Using JPEG for Icons
docs.text:
<img src="icon.jpg" alt="Icon" width="24" height="24">

Why it's wrong: JPEG is bad for icons.

✅ Correct: Use SVG or PNG.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Not Compressing Images
docs.text:
<img src="photo-4000-raw.jpg" alt="Photo">

Why it's wrong: Bloated files.

✅ Correct: Compress to ~80% quality.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: No CDN
docs.text:
Why it's wrong: Slow global delivery.

✅ Correct: Use a CDN.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Autoplay Video Unmuted
docs.text:
<video autoplay>

Why it's wrong: Wastes bandwidth, hostile to users.

✅ Correct: autoplay muted playsinline.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: preload="auto" for Videos
docs.text:
<video preload="auto">

Why it's wrong: Downloads the entire video upfront.

✅ Correct: preload="none".

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: No Video Poster
docs.text:
<video preload="none">

Why it's wrong: Blank space before playback.

✅ Correct: Add poster.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: No font-display: swap
docs.text:
@font-face {
    font-family: 'Custom';
    src: url('font.woff2');
}

Why it's wrong: Invisible text (FOIT).

✅ Correct: 

@font-face {
    font-family: 'Custom';
    src: url('font.woff2');
    font-display: swap;
}

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Not Testing on Real Devices
docs.text:
Why it's wrong: Emulators miss real-world issues.

✅ Correct: Test on real phones.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Ignoring Core Web Vitals
docs.text:
Why it's wrong: Hurts SEO and UX.

✅ Correct: Monitor and improve.

docs.title: 13. Performance Considerations
docs.text:
• Weight – reduce bytes.
  • Requests – reduce count.
  • LCP – preload and prioritise.
  • CLS – set dimensions.
  • INP – use async decoding.
  • Compression – reduce file size.
  • Caching – long cache lifetimes.
  • CDN – global delivery.
  • Format – modern formats.
  • Lazy loading – defer off-screen.
  • HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 – multiplexing.
  • Brotli – better compression than gzip.
  • Fonts – subset and preload.
  • SVG – optimise with SVGO.

docs.title: Performance Tips
docs.text:
1. Audit with Lighthouse.
  2. Set performance budgets.
  3. Use modern formats.
  4. Compress aggressively.
  5. Lazy load.
  6. Set dimensions.
  7. Preload LCP.
  8. Use a CDN.
  9. Cache aggressively.
  10. Monitor RUM.

docs.title: 14. Security Considerations
docs.text:
• CORS – use crossorigin for cross-origin media.
  • HTTPS – required for secure playback.
  • CSP – restrict media sources with img-src, media-src, frame-src.
  • Mixed content – HTTPS pages must load HTTPS media.
  • Malicious files – validate user uploads.
  • EXIF data – strip GPS coordinates.
  • SVG injection – sanitize user SVG.
  • Hotlinking – use referrer policy or CDN.

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use HTTPS – for all media.
  2. Set CSP – restrict sources.
  3. Sanitize uploads – validate file type and content.
  4. Strip EXIF – for user images.
  5. Use crossorigin – for cross-origin.

docs.title: 15. Debugging Tips
docs.text:
• DevTools Network panel – inspect media requests.
  • Coverage panel – see unused bytes.
  • Performance panel – inspect LCP, CLS, INP.
  • Lighthouse – audits.
  • PageSpeed Insights – field + lab data.
  • WebPageTest – detailed waterfall.
  • performance.getEntriesByType('resource') – resource timings.
  • PerformanceObserver – LCP, CLS, INP.
  • CrUX – real-user metrics.
  • RUM – custom monitoring.

docs.title: 16. When to Use
docs.text:
• For every website – media performance is universal.
  • For e-commerce – product images.
  • For news – hero images, videos.
  • For blogs – images.
  • For galleries – many images.
  • For mobile – bandwidth and battery.
  • For SEO – Core Web Vitals.

docs.title: 17. When Not to Use
docs.text:
• Never – media performance is always relevant.
  • Exception: tiny sites with minimal media — but even then, basic optimisations apply.

docs.title: 18. Related Concepts
docs.text:
• Core Web Vitals – LCP, CLS, INP.
  • Responsive images – srcset, sizes.
  • <picture> – art direction + format fallback.
  • Lazy loading – loading="lazy".
  • Resource hints – preload, preconnect, prefetch.
  • Image formats – AVIF, WebP, JPEG, PNG, SVG.
  • Video formats – H.264, VP9, AV1.
  • CDN – global delivery.
  • Caching – HTTP cache, Service Workers.
  • content-visibility – skip rendering.
  • fetchpriority – priority hints.
  • decoding – sync/async.
  • PerformanceObserver – metrics.
  • Lighthouse – audits.
  • CrUX – real-user metrics.
  • RUM – Real User Monitoring.

docs.title: 19. Did You Know?
docs.text:
• Images account for ~50% of a typical page's weight.

  • Video can push a page past several MB — often the heaviest resource.

  • AVIF offers up to 50% better compression than JPEG.

  • WebP offers 25–35% better compression than JPEG.

  • Lazy loading can reduce initial load by 30–60%.

  • Responsive images can save 50–80% of bandwidth on mobile.

  • Core Web Vitals became a ranking signal in 2021.

  • LCP should be ≤ 2.5 seconds; CLS ≤ 0.1; INP ≤ 200 ms.

  • Preloading the LCP image can reduce LCP by 200–800 ms.

  • Setting image dimensions prevents CLS entirely.

  • decoding="async" decodes images off the main thread.

  • content-visibility: auto skips rendering off-screen content.

  • A CDN can reduce latency by 50% or more for global users.

  • Brotli compresses text and SVG better than gzip.

  • Font subsetting can reduce font files by 80% or more.

  • Service Workers enable offline and fast repeat views.

  • Lighthouse audits and scores media performance.

  • CrUX provides real-user metrics from Chrome users.

  • RUM (Real User Monitoring) captures field data.

  • Best practices include modern formats, responsive images, lazy loading, dimensions, and preload.

  • Common mistakes include large images, no dimensions, lazy-loading LCP, no preload.

  • Following best practices for media performance leads to faster, more accessible, and more successful websites.

docs.title: 20. Summary
docs.text:
• Media performance is the practice of optimising images, video, audio, and SVG for speed.
  • Core Web Vitals (LCP, CLS, INP) are the primary metrics.
  • Modern formats (AVIF, WebP) reduce file size significantly.
  • Responsive images (srcset, sizes) serve the right size.
  • Lazy loading (loading="lazy") defers off-screen media.
  • Dimensions (width/height) prevent CLS.
  • Preload the LCP image with fetchpriority="high".
  • Resource hints (preconnect, preload, prefetch) speed up loading.
  • CDNs and caching enable global, fast delivery.
  • Best practices: modern formats, responsive images, lazy loading, dimensions, preload.
  • Common mistakes include large images, no dimensions, lazy-loading LCP, no preload.
  • Media performance is essential for speed, SEO, conversion, and user experience.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
The <iframe> element (short for inline frame) is an HTML element that embeds another HTML document inside the current document. It creates a nested browsing context — a fully independent window that renders its own document, with its own URL, its own JavaScript execution context, its own DOM, and its own CSS scope. The embedded document is completely isolated from the parent page, except for controlled communication channels.

Iframes are used to embed content from other sources — YouTube videos, Google Maps, social media posts, ads, payment forms, and third-party widgets — without integrating their code directly into the parent page. They are also used for sandboxing untrusted content, isolating third-party scripts, and preventing CSS/JS conflicts.

Example: 

<iframe src="https://example.com/embed"
        width="800"
        height="450"
        title="Embedded content"
        loading="lazy">
</iframe>

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
The <iframe> element serves several essential purposes:

  • Embedding external content – YouTube, Vimeo, Google Maps, social embeds.
  • Sandboxing untrusted content – isolating third-party code.
  • Isolating CSS and JavaScript – preventing conflicts with the parent page.
  • Third-party widgets – payment forms (Stripe, PayPal), chat widgets, ads.
  • Legacy integration – embedding older applications.
  • Micro-frontends – composing independent applications.
  • Security boundaries – enforcing same-origin isolation.
  • Progressive loading – deferring heavy third-party content.

docs.title: Where It Fits
docs.text:
The <iframe> element is embedded content, flow content, and phrasing content. It is a replaced element that creates a nested browsing context. It can appear anywhere phrasing content is accepted — inside <p>, <div>, <section>, <figure>, <td>, and more.

<figure>
    <iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/VIDEO_ID"
            width="800"
            height="450"
            title="Tutorial video"
            loading="lazy"
            allowfullscreen>
    </iframe>
    <figcaption>Video: Getting Started with HTML</figcaption>
</figure>

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text:
Before <iframe>, embedding content from another document required either:

  1. Copying the content – which broke isolation, licensing, and updates.
  2. Using <frame> and <frameset> – the original HTML frameset model, which was rigid and problematic.
  3. Server-side includes (SSI) – which only worked for same-origin content.
  4. JavaScript-based solutions – which required CORS and were fragile.

Developers needed a way to embed an entire independent document inside another page, with isolation, independence, and composability. The <frameset> model was too rigid — it split the window into fixed panes and couldn't be embedded within content. A more flexible solution was needed.

docs.title: Previous Limitations
docs.text: Limitation Consequence <frameset> only Rigid full-page layout, not embeddable Server-side includes Same-origin only Copying content No isolation, no updates, licensing issues JavaScript embeds Required CORS, fragile, no isolation No sandboxing Third-party code had full access CSS/JS conflicts Third-party styles broke parent page Security risks Third-party scripts could access everything

docs.title: Why the <iframe> Element Was Introduced
docs.text:
The <iframe> element was introduced in HTML 4.0 (1997) (and supported earlier in Internet Explorer 3) as a flexible, embeddable, isolated browsing context. It was designed to:

  • Embed documents – any HTML document, from any origin.
  • Provide isolation – separate DOM, JS, and CSS.
  • Enforce same-origin policy – security boundary.
  • Be embeddable within content – unlike <frameset>.
  • Support scripting – parent-child communication via postMessage.
  • Enable third-party integration – ads, widgets, videos.

Over time, iframes gained powerful security features:

  • sandbox attribute (HTML5) – restricts capabilities.
  • allow attribute – controls feature permissions.
  • referrerpolicy – controls referrer information.
  • csp attribute – Content Security Policy for the iframe.
  • credentialless – cookie-less embedding.

The <iframe> element remains the only way to embed a full external document with browser-enforced isolation.

docs.title: The Basic Syntax of <iframe>
docs.text:
<iframe src="URL" title="Description" width="800" height="450"></iframe>
  • src – the URL of the document to embed.
  • title – required for accessibility (describes the iframe).
  • width / height – dimensions.

docs.title: Simple Iframe
docs.text: <iframe src="https://example.com" title="Example website" width="800" height="450"></iframe>

docs.title: YouTube Embed
docs.text:
<iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ"
        title="YouTube video player"
        width="800"
        height="450"
        loading="lazy"
        allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture"
        allowfullscreen>
</iframe>

docs.title: Google Maps Embed
docs.text:
<iframe src="https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=..."
        title="Map of New York"
        width="800"
        height="450"
        loading="lazy"
        referrerpolicy="no-referrer-when-downgrade"
        allowfullscreen>
</iframe>

docs.title: Lazy-Loaded Iframe
docs.text:
<iframe src="https://example.com/embed"
        title="Embedded content"
        loading="lazy"
        width="800"
        height="450">
</iframe>

docs.title: Sandboxed Iframe
docs.text:
<iframe src="https://untrusted.com"
        title="Untrusted content"
        sandbox
        width="800"
        height="450">
</iframe>

sandbox with no value applies the most restrictive policy (no scripts, no forms, no popups, no navigation).

docs.title: Sandbox with Permissions
docs.text:
<iframe src="https://untrusted.com"
        title="Untrusted content"
        sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-forms"
        width="800"
        height="450">
</iframe>

docs.title: Feature Policy with allow
docs.text:
<iframe src="https://example.com"
        title="Camera app"
        allow="camera; microphone; geolocation"
        width="800"
        height="450">
</iframe>

docs.title: Iframe with srcdoc
docs.text:
<iframe srcdoc="<h1>Hello, World!</h1><p>This is inline HTML.</p>"
        title="Inline content"
        width="800"
        height="450">
</iframe>

docs.title: Iframe with postMessage Communication
docs.text:
Parent: 

<iframe id="child" src="https://example.com/embed" title="Child"></iframe>
<script>
    const child = document.getElementById('child');
    child.contentWindow.postMessage('Hello from parent!', 'https://example.com');
    window.addEventListener('message', (event) => {
        if (event.origin === 'https://example.com') {
            console.log('From child:', event.data);
        }
    });
</script>

Child: 

<script>
    window.addEventListener('message', (event) => {
        if (event.origin === 'https://parent.com') {
            console.log('From parent:', event.data);
            event.source.postMessage('Hello from child!', event.origin);
        }
    });
</script>

docs.title: Code Breakdown
docs.text: Attribute Purpose src The URL of the document to embed srcdoc Inline HTML content (overrides src) title Accessible description (required) width / height Dimensions loading lazy or eager sandbox Restricts capabilities allow Feature permissions allowfullscreen Allows fullscreen referrerpolicy Controls referrer csp Content Security Policy name Name for targeting allowtransparency Legacy; use CSS instead credentialless Cookie-less embedding

docs.title: The "Picture-in-Picture TV" Analogy
docs.text: Think of an <iframe> as a picture-in-picture TV embedded in a larger screen. The small TV shows its own channel (its own document) completely independently of the main screen. It has its own controls, its own content, and its own rules. The two are visible at once but operate separately.

docs.title: The "Nested Browsing Context" Mental Model
docs.text:
The most accurate mental model: an iframe creates a browser within a browser. The embedded document:

  • Has its own URL.
  • Has its own DOM.
  • Has its own JavaScript execution context (separate global scope).
  • Has its own CSS scope (parent styles don't cascade in).
  • Has its own history (back/forward may not affect it).
  • Is subject to the same-origin policy (isolated from the parent unless same origin).

docs.title: The "Ship in a Bottle" Analogy
docs.text: An iframe is like a ship in a bottle — a complete, self-contained world inside a larger container. You can see it, interact with it through limited channels (postMessage), but you can't reach inside and rearrange its furniture (unless same-origin).

docs.title: The "Sandbox" Mental Model
docs.text: The sandbox attribute is like a child's sandbox — the child (embedded content) plays in a contained area with limited tools. They can't wander into the rest of the house, can't open drawers, and can't change the rules. The parent controls what tools (permissions) the child has.

docs.title: The "Apartment Building" Mental Model
docs.text: Think of a page as an apartment building. Each iframe is a separate apartment with its own door, its own furniture, and its own rules. Neighbors can talk through the intercom (postMessage), but they can't walk into each other's apartments unless the doors are unlocked (same-origin).

docs.title: The "Frame vs. Iframe" Mental Model
docs.text:
• <frameset>/<frame> – divides the browser window into panes. Obsolete.
  • <iframe> – embeds a document inline within content. Modern and flexible.

Iframe replaced frameset because it can be embedded in the middle of a page, not just at the top level.

docs.title: Concept 1: The src Attribute
docs.text:
The src attribute specifies the URL of the document to embed:

<iframe src="https://example.com"></iframe>

Note: Loading is asynchronous. The parent page continues rendering while the iframe loads.

docs.title: Concept 2: The srcdoc Attribute
docs.text:
The srcdoc attribute embeds an inline HTML document:

<iframe srcdoc="<p>Hello, World!</p>"></iframe>

Use case: Small, self-contained documents without a separate file.

Note: srcdoc overrides src.

docs.title: Concept 3: The title Attribute (Required)
docs.text:
The title attribute provides an accessible name for the iframe:

<iframe src="..." title="YouTube video player"></iframe>

Why: Screen readers announce the title when the user navigates to the iframe. Without it, the iframe is announced as "frame" with no context.

WCAG 4.1.2 (Name, Role, Value) requires the iframe to have a title.

docs.title: Concept 4: The sandbox Attribute
docs.text:
The sandbox attribute applies a set of restrictions to the embedded content:

<iframe src="..." sandbox></iframe>

Default (no value): Most restrictive — disables: - Scripts. - Forms. - Popups. - Top-level navigation. - Plugins. - Same-origin (forces unique origin). - Pointer lock. - Presentation. - Downloads (in some browsers).

Permissions (add to enable):

Token Allows allow-scripts JavaScript execution allow-same-origin Same-origin access allow-forms Form submission allow-popups Popups allow-top-navigation Navigate the top page allow-top-navigation-by-user-activation Top navigation on user action allow-modals Alert, confirm, prompt allow-orientation-lock Screen orientation lock allow-pointer-lock Pointer lock API allow-presentation Presentation API allow-downloads File downloads allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox Popups not sandboxed

Critical warning: allow-scripts + allow-same-origin together nullifies the sandbox — the iframe can remove its own sandbox attribute. Never use both for untrusted content from the same origin.

docs.title: Concept 5: The allow Attribute
docs.text:
The allow attribute controls feature permissions (formerly Feature Policy, now Permissions Policy):

<iframe src="..." allow="camera; microphone; geolocation"></iframe>

Common permissions:

  • camera
  • microphone
  • geolocation
  • payment
  • autoplay
  • encrypted-media
  • fullscreen
  • picture-in-picture
  • clipboard-read
  • clipboard-write

docs.title: Concept 6: The referrerpolicy Attribute
docs.text:
Controls the Referer header sent when the iframe loads:

<iframe src="..." referrerpolicy="no-referrer"></iframe>

Values: no-referrer, no-referrer-when-downgrade, origin, origin-when-cross-origin, same-origin, strict-origin, strict-origin-when-cross-origin, unsafe-url.

docs.title: Concept 7: The csp Attribute
docs.text:
Sets a Content Security Policy for the embedded document:

<iframe src="..." csp="default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'"></iframe>

Note: Experimental; browser support varies.

docs.title: Concept 8: The loading Attribute
docs.text:
Defers loading of off-screen iframes:

<iframe src="..." loading="lazy"></iframe>

Values: lazy, eager.

docs.title: Concept 9: The allowfullscreen Attribute
docs.text:
Allows the embedded content to enter fullscreen:

<iframe src="..." allowfullscreen></iframe>

Note: Also needs to be allowed via allow="fullscreen" in some browsers.

docs.title: Concept 10: The Same-Origin Policy
docs.text:
Iframes are subject to the same-origin policy:

  • Same origin – full access (DOM, JS).
  • Cross-origin – limited access; only postMessage communication.

An origin is defined by scheme + host + port:

  • https://example.com/page1 and https://example.com/page2 — same origin.
  • https://example.com and https://other.com — different origin.
  • http://example.com and https://example.com — different origin (scheme).
  • https://example.com:443 and https://example.com:8443 — different origin (port).

docs.title: Concept 11: Cross-Origin Communication (postMessage)
docs.text:
For cross-origin iframes, communication happens via postMessage:

iframe.contentWindow.postMessage(message, targetOrigin);

Security: Always specify targetOrigin and check event.origin:

window.addEventListener('message', (event) => {
    if (event.origin !== 'https://trusted.com') return;
    // Handle message
});

docs.title: Concept 12: Same-Origin Access
docs.text:
For same-origin iframes, the parent can access the iframe's DOM:

const iframeDoc = iframe.contentDocument;
const iframeWin = iframe.contentWindow;
iframeDoc.body.style.background = 'red';

Note: Cross-origin access throws a SecurityError.

docs.title: Concept 13: The contentWindow and contentDocument
docs.text: Property Description iframe.contentWindow The Window object of the iframe iframe.contentDocument The Document object of the iframe (same-origin only)

docs.title: Concept 14: Iframe and CSP
docs.text:
The Content-Security-Policy HTTP header can restrict iframes:

  • frame-ancestors – who can embed this page.
  • frame-src – what sources the page can embed.
Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'

Why: Prevents clickjacking (embedding your page in an attacker's iframe).

docs.title: Concept 15: Iframe and Clickjacking
docs.text:
Clickjacking is an attack where the attacker embeds your site in a transparent iframe and tricks users into clicking invisible buttons.

Protection:

  • X-Frame-Options: DENY – no embedding.
  • X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN – same-origin only.
  • CSP frame-ancestors – more flexible.

docs.title: Concept 16: Iframe and X-Frame-Options
docs.text:
The X-Frame-Options HTTP header controls embedding:

Value Behaviour DENY Never embed SAMEORIGIN Same-origin only ALLOW-FROM uri Specific origin (deprecated)

docs.title: Concept 17: Iframe and Performance
docs.text:
• Separate document – extra HTTP request, extra parse, extra render.
  • Extra memory – each iframe is a browsing context.
  • Main thread – same-origin iframes share the event loop; cross-origin use separate processes.
  • Blocking – iframes can delay page load if not lazy-loaded.
  • Sandboxing cost – sandboxed iframes may be slower.

docs.title: Concept 18: Iframe and SEO
docs.text:
• Content inside iframes is not indexed as part of the parent (mostly).
  • Iframe content is indexed separately (if publicly accessible).
  • Avoid using iframes for critical content.
  • Provide alternative content for SEO.

docs.title: Concept 19: Iframe Accessibility
docs.text:
• title attribute is required for accessibility.
  • Avoid tabbing traps – ensure users can tab out.
  • Ensure iframe content is accessible.
  • Consider role="application" for interactive apps.
  • Provide alternative content for screen readers if needed.

docs.title: Concept 20: Iframe and Mobile
docs.text:
• On mobile, iframes can be slow and hard to interact with.
  • Use loading="lazy".
  • Consider replacing iframes with links on mobile.

docs.title: Concept 21: The name Attribute
docs.text:
The name attribute allows the iframe to be a target for links and forms:

<iframe name="result"></iframe>
<form target="result">...</form>
<a href="page.html" target="result">Load in iframe</a>

docs.title: Concept 22: Iframes for Micro-Frontends
docs.text:
Iframes are used to compose micro-frontends — independently deployed applications:

<iframe src="https://team-a.example.com/widget" title="Team A widget"></iframe>
<iframe src="https://team-b.example.com/widget" title="Team B widget"></iframe>

docs.title: Concept 23: Iframes for Payment Forms
docs.text:
Payment providers (Stripe, PayPal, Adyen) use iframes to isolate card data from the merchant page:

<iframe src="https://js.stripe.com/v3/elements-inner-card-..." title="Card payment"></iframe>

Benefit: PCI compliance — card data never touches the merchant's servers.

docs.title: Concept 24: Iframes for Ads
docs.text:
Ads are often served in iframes to:

  • Isolate untrusted ad scripts.
  • Prevent ad CSS from breaking the page.
  • Enforce security boundaries.

docs.title: Concept 25: Iframe and History
docs.text:
• Same-origin iframes – their navigation adds to the parent's history.
  • Cross-origin iframes – their navigation does not (mostly).
  • window.history – the iframe can manipulate its own history.

docs.title: Step-by-Step: Browser Processing an Iframe
docs.text:
1.  Browser parses the `<iframe>` element.
    │
    ▼
2.  It creates a **nested browsing context**.
    │
    ▼
3.  It reads the attributes: `src`, `sandbox`, `allow`, etc.
    │
    ▼
4.  If `srcdoc` is present, the inline document is used.
    │
    ▼
5.  If `src` is present, the browser fetches the URL:
    │   ├── Check cache.
    │   ├── Resolve DNS.
    │   ├── Establish connection.
    │   └── Fetch document.
    │
    ▼
6.  Apply sandbox restrictions.
    │
    ▼
7.  Parse the embedded document.
    │
    ▼
8.  Build the iframe's DOM.
    │
    ▼
9.  Load resources (CSS, images).
    │
    ▼
10. Render the iframe content.
    │
    ▼
11. Fire the `load` event on the iframe.
    │
    ▼
12. Parent and child can communicate (same-origin directly; cross-origin via postMessage).

docs.title: Sandbox Behaviour
docs.text:
When the sandbox attribute is present:

  1. The iframe is treated as a unique opaque origin (unless allow-same-origin).
  2. Scripts are disabled (unless allow-scripts).
  3. Forms are disabled (unless allow-forms).
  4. Popups are disabled (unless allow-popups).
  5. Top-level navigation is disabled (unless allow-top-navigation).

docs.title: Same-Origin Access Flow
docs.text:
Parent page (https://example.com)
    │
    ▼
iframe src="https://example.com/child"
    │
    ▼
Same origin → parent.contentDocument → access granted

docs.title: Cross-Origin Access Flow
docs.text:
Parent page (https://example.com)
    │
    ▼
iframe src="https://other.com/child"
    │
    ▼
Different origin → parent.contentDocument → SecurityError
    │
    ▼
Only postMessage communication allowed

docs.title: The postMessage Protocol
docs.text:
Parent → child:
    child.contentWindow.postMessage(data, 'https://other.com')

Child → parent:
    window.parent.postMessage(data, 'https://example.com')

Both must verify origin:
    event.origin === expected

docs.title: Sandbox and CSP Interaction
docs.text:
Sandboxing intersects with CSP:

  • CSP frame-ancestors – controls who can embed the page.
  • CSP sandbox directive – applies sandbox to the embedding.
  • sandbox attribute – applies sandbox to the iframe.

docs.title: The Iframe in the DOM
docs.text:
const iframe = document.querySelector('iframe');
console.log(iframe.contentWindow);   // The iframe's Window
console.log(iframe.contentDocument); // The iframe's Document (same-origin)
console.log(iframe.src);              // The URL
console.log(iframe.sandbox);          // The sandbox attribute

docs.title: Accessibility Tree
docs.text:
Iframes are exposed as:

  • role: iframe or document (varies).
  • name: from title attribute.

Screen readers announce the title and allow navigation into the iframe.

docs.title: The HTMLIFrameElement Interface
docs.text: Property Description src The URL srcdoc Inline HTML name Frame name sandbox Sandbox tokens allow Feature permissions allowFullscreen Fullscreen flag allowPaymentRequest Payment request flag referrerPolicy Referrer policy csp Content Security Policy contentWindow The iframe's Window contentDocument The iframe's Document (same-origin) width Width height Height loading lazy or eager

docs.title: The Nested Browsing Context
docs.text:
The iframe creates a nested browsing context — a separate environment with:

  • Its own Window object.
  • Its own Document object.
  • Its own JavaScript global scope.
  • Its own history.
  • Its own security origin.

docs.title: Origin Isolation
docs.text:
• Same-origin iframes run in the same process (in some browsers).
  • Cross-origin iframes run in separate processes (process isolation).
  • site isolation — modern browsers isolate each site in its own process.

Benefit: A compromised iframe cannot access the parent's memory.

docs.title: Sandbox Implementation
docs.text:
The sandbox attribute is enforced by the browser:

  • Unique origin – the iframe gets an opaque origin.
  • Feature restrictions – the specified features are disabled.

The sandbox is enforced at the browsing context level, affecting navigation, scripting, and storage.

docs.title: CSP frame-ancestors
docs.text:
The CSP frame-ancestors directive tells the browser who may embed the page:

Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' https://trusted.com

The browser checks this before rendering the iframe.

docs.title: The X-Frame-Options Header
docs.text:
Older header for clickjacking protection:

X-Frame-Options: DENY
X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN

Note: frame-ancestors supersedes X-Frame-Options in modern browsers.

docs.title: Iframe Loading and Priority
docs.text:
• loading="lazy" – defers off-screen iframes.
  • fetchpriority – not applicable to iframes.
  • Same-origin iframes – loaded with the parent's priority.
  • Cross-origin iframes – lower priority.

docs.title: The sandbox Iframe Restrictions
docs.text:
When sandbox is applied, the iframe:

  • Is assigned a unique opaque origin (unless allow-same-origin).
  • Cannot access cookies, localStorage, or IndexedDB.
  • Cannot open popups.
  • Cannot submit forms.
  • Cannot run scripts.
  • Cannot navigate the top page.
  • Cannot use plugins.
  • Cannot use pointer lock.

docs.title: Sandbox Escape Warning
docs.text: Never combine allow-scripts with allow-same-origin for untrusted content. The combination removes the sandbox because the script can access document.body.parentNode and remove the sandbox attribute.

docs.title: Cross-Origin Communication Security
docs.text:
postMessage includes:

  • data – the message.
  • targetOrigin – required to prevent leakage.
  • event.origin – the sender's origin.
  • event.source – a reference to the sender's window.

Always specify targetOrigin and verify event.origin.

docs.title: The Lifecycle of an Iframe
docs.text:
1.  Author writes `<iframe src="..." title="...">`.
    │
    ▼
2.  File deployed.
    │
    ▼
3.  Browser parses HTML.
    │
    ▼
4.  Browser creates a nested browsing context.
    │
    ▼
5.  Browser fetches the iframe document.
    │
    ▼
6.  Browser parses the document.
    │
    ▼
7.  Browser applies sandbox restrictions.
    │
    ▼
8.  Browser builds the iframe's DOM.
    │
    ▼
9.  Browser loads iframe resources.
    │
    ▼
10. Browser renders iframe content.
    │
    ▼
11. `load` event fires on the iframe.
    │
    ▼
12. Parent and child communicate (postMessage or same-origin).
    │
    ▼
13. User interacts with iframe content.
    │
    ▼
14. Iframe navigation updates its own history.
    │
    ▼
15. When the page is unloaded, the iframe is destroyed.

docs.title: Dynamic Iframe Creation
docs.text:
const iframe = document.createElement('iframe');
iframe.src = 'https://example.com';
iframe.title = 'Embedded content';
iframe.width = '800';
iframe.height = '450';
iframe.loading = 'lazy';
document.body.appendChild(iframe);

docs.title: Removing an Iframe
docs.text: iframe.remove(); // Removes from DOM; browsing context destroyed

docs.title: Iframe Navigation
docs.text:
iframe.src = 'https://example.com/new-page';
// Or
iframe.contentWindow.location.href = 'https://example.com/new-page'; // Same-origin only

docs.title: Example 1: Simple Iframe
docs.text: <iframe src="https://example.com" title="Example website" width="800" height="450"></iframe>

docs.title: Example 2: YouTube Embed
docs.text:
<iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ"
        title="YouTube video player"
        width="800"
        height="450"
        loading="lazy"
        allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture"
        allowfullscreen>
</iframe>

docs.title: Example 3: Google Maps Embed
docs.text:
<iframe src="https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=!1m18!1m12!1m3!1d3022.5!2d-73.9857!3d40.7484"
        title="Map of the Empire State Building"
        width="800"
        height="450"
        loading="lazy"
        referrerpolicy="no-referrer-when-downgrade"
        allowfullscreen>
</iframe>

docs.title: Example 4: Sandboxed Iframe (Most Restrictive)
docs.text:
<iframe src="https://untrusted.com"
        title="Untrusted content"
        sandbox
        width="800"
        height="450">
</iframe>

docs.title: Example 5: Sandboxed Iframe with Scripts
docs.text:
<iframe src="https://untrusted.com"
        title="Untrusted content with scripts"
        sandbox="allow-scripts"
        width="800"
        height="450">
</iframe>

Note: No allow-same-origin — the iframe has a unique origin.

docs.title: Example 6: Sandboxed Iframe with Forms
docs.text:
<iframe src="https://untrusted.com/form"
        title="Embedded form"
        sandbox="allow-forms"
        width="800"
        height="450">
</iframe>

docs.title: Example 7: Iframe with Feature Permissions
docs.text:
<iframe src="https://example.com/camera-app"
        title="Camera app"
        allow="camera; microphone; fullscreen"
        width="800"
        height="450">
</iframe>

docs.title: Example 8: Lazy-Loaded Iframe
docs.text:
<iframe src="https://example.com/embed"
        title="Embedded content"
        loading="lazy"
        width="800"
        height="450">
</iframe>

docs.title: Example 9: Iframe with srcdoc
docs.text:
<iframe srcdoc="<h1>Hello, World!</h1><p>This is inline HTML.</p>"
        title="Inline content"
        width="800"
        height="450">
</iframe>

docs.title: Example 10: Iframe with postMessage (Parent)
docs.text:
<iframe id="child" src="https://example.com/embed" title="Child iframe"></iframe>
<script>
    const child = document.getElementById('child');
    child.addEventListener('load', () => {
        child.contentWindow.postMessage('Hello from parent!', 'https://example.com');
    });
    window.addEventListener('message', (event) => {
        if (event.origin !== 'https://example.com') return;
        console.log('From child:', event.data);
    });
</script>

docs.title: Example 11: Iframe with postMessage (Child)
docs.text:
<script>
    window.addEventListener('message', (event) => {
        if (event.origin !== 'https://parent.com') return;
        console.log('From parent:', event.data);
        event.source.postMessage('Hello back!', event.origin);
    });
</script>

docs.title: Example 12: Same-Origin Iframe Access
docs.text:
<iframe id="myFrame" src="/child.html" title="Child"></iframe>
<script>
    const iframe = document.getElementById('myFrame');
    iframe.addEventListener('load', () => {
        const doc = iframe.contentDocument;
        doc.body.style.background = 'lightblue';
        doc.querySelector('h1').textContent = 'Updated from parent!';
    });
</script>

docs.title: Example 13: Iframe as a Link Target
docs.text:
<a href="page1.html" target="myFrame">Page 1</a>
<a href="page2.html" target="myFrame">Page 2</a>
<iframe name="myFrame" src="page1.html" title="Content viewer" width="800" height="450"></iframe>

docs.title: Example 14: Iframe with X-Frame-Options (Server-Side)
docs.text:
X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN

Prevents other sites from embedding your page.

docs.title: Example 15: Iframe with CSP frame-ancestors (Server-Side)
docs.text:
Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' https://trusted.com

Only self and trusted.com can embed your page.

docs.title: Example 16: Iframe with frame-src CSP
docs.text:
Content-Security-Policy: frame-src https://www.youtube.com https://www.google.com

Restricts what sources the page can embed.

docs.title: Example 17: Iframe with Stripe (Payment)
docs.text:
<div id="card-element"></div>
<script src="https://js.stripe.com/v3/"></script>
<script>
    const stripe = Stripe('pk_test_...');
    const elements = stripe.elements();
    const card = elements.create('card');
    card.mount('#card-element');
</script>

Note: Stripe Elements uses an iframe internally for PCI compliance.

docs.title: Example 18: Iframe Sandbox for Ad
docs.text:
<iframe src="https://ad.example.com/ad"
        title="Advertisement"
        sandbox="allow-scripts allow-popups"
        width="300"
        height="250"
        loading="lazy">
</iframe>

docs.title: Example 19: Iframe with credentialless
docs.text:
<iframe src="https://untrusted.com"
        title="Untrusted content"
        credentialless
        width="800"
        height="450">
</iframe>

Note: credentialless is experimental; it loads the iframe in a new, ephemeral context with no credentials.

docs.title: Example 20: Complete Iframe Demo
docs.text:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>Iframe Demo</title>
    <style>
        body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; max-width: 900px; margin: 2rem auto; padding: 0 1rem; }
        iframe { width: 100%; height: 450px; border: 1px solid #dee2e6; border-radius: 8px; }
        section { margin-bottom: 2rem; }
        .lazy-container { position: relative; }
        .video-wrapper { position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; }
        .video-wrapper iframe { position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; }
    </style>
</head>
<body>
    <h1>Iframe Demo</h1>

    <section>
        <h2>YouTube Embed (Responsive)</h2>
        <div class="video-wrapper">
            <iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ"
                    title="YouTube video player"
                    loading="lazy"
                    allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture"
                    allowfullscreen>
            </iframe>
        </div>
    </section>

    <section>
        <h2>Google Maps Embed</h2>
        <iframe src="https://www.google.com/maps/embed?pb=!1m18!1m12!1m3!1d3022.5!2d-73.9857!3d40.7484"
                title="Map of New York"
                loading="lazy"
                referrerpolicy="no-referrer-when-downgrade"
                allowfullscreen>
        </iframe>
    </section>

    <section>
        <h2>Sandboxed Iframe</h2>
        <iframe srcdoc="<h2>Sandboxed Content</h2><p>Scripts are disabled.</p><script>alert('Not run!')</script>"
                title="Sandboxed content"
                sandbox>
        </iframe>
    </section>

    <section>
        <h2>Inline HTML with `srcdoc`</h2>
        <iframe srcdoc="<h2>Inline Content</h2><p>This is rendered from the srcdoc attribute.</p><style>h2 { color: #3498db; }</style>"
                title="Inline content">
        </iframe>
    </section>
</body>
</html>

docs.title: 10. Common Use Cases
docs.text: Use Case Example Video embeds YouTube, Vimeo Maps Google Maps, OpenStreetMap Social media Tweets, Facebook posts Ads Display ads (isolated) Payment forms Stripe, PayPal Chat widgets Intercom, Drift Code playgrounds CodePen, JSFiddle Micro-frontends Independently deployed widgets Documentation Embedded examples Analytics dashboards Grafana, Tableau CMS previews Live preview of content Sandboxed untrusted content User-submitted HTML

docs.title: 11. Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Always include title – required for accessibility.
  2. Use loading="lazy" – for off-screen iframes.
  3. Use sandbox – for untrusted content.
  4. Never use allow-scripts + allow-same-origin together – nullifies sandbox.
