docs.title: 19. Did You Know?
docs.text:
• The <template> element was introduced as part of the Web Components specification in 2011.
  • Template content is stored in a DocumentFragment — not in the template element itself.
  • template.children is empty — the content is in template.content.
  • template.innerHTML returns an empty string — the content is not in the template.
  • Template content is inert — scripts do not run, images do not load, styles do not apply.
  • The template contents owner document is separate — this is what makes the content inert.
  • Templates are parsed once, cloned many times — faster than string concatenation.
  • cloneNode(true) deep clones — false shallow clones.
  • DocumentFragment batches DOM mutations — one operation for many clones.
  • Declarative Shadow DOM uses <template shadowrootmode="open">.
  • shadowrootdelegatesfocus enables focus delegation.
  • shadowrootclonable allows cloning the shadow root.
  • shadowrootserializable allows serializing the shadow root.
  • Declarative Shadow DOM is supported in Chrome 90+, Edge 90+, Safari 16.4+, Firefox 123+.
  • Most frameworks use templates internally — Lit, Vue, Angular, Svelte.
  • React uses JSX, not <template> — but the concept is similar.
  • Templates are safe to hold untrusted markup — content is inert.
  • Cloning a template does not sanitize content — sanitize before inserting.
  • <template> is not the same as <div hidden> — hidden elements are rendered (then hidden).
  • <template> is not the same as <script type="text/template"> — the script hack is obsolete.
  • Templates are the foundation of Web Components — every component starts with a template.
  • The template element is a unique primitive — no other element has inert content.
  • The best template is the one you never have to modify — write once, clone many.

docs.title: 20. Summary
docs.text:
• The <template> element holds markup that is parsed but not rendered.
  • The content lives in template.content — a DocumentFragment.
  • template.children and template.innerHTML are empty — the content is not in the template element.
  • Template content is inert — scripts do not run, images do not load.
  • Instantiate templates with template.content.cloneNode(true).
  • Modify the clone before inserting it into the DOM.
  • Batch clones with a DocumentFragment — one DOM operation for many.
  • Templates are faster than string concatenation — parsed once, cloned cheaply.
  • Templates are the foundation of Web Components.
  • Declarative Shadow DOM uses <template shadowrootmode="open">.
  • shadowrootdelegatesfocus, shadowrootclonable, and shadowrootserializable extend declarative shadow DOM.
  • Templates work with slots for content projection.
  • Templates are supported in all modern browsers.
  • Templates are used in most frameworks — Lit, Vue, Angular, Svelte.
  • Do not use template.innerHTML — use template.content.
  • Do not forget to clone — always clone before insertion.
  • Do not put scripts in templates expecting them to run — they run on insertion.
  • Do not use templates for hidden content — use <div hidden>.
  • Templates are the declarative way to define reusable markup.
  • The best template is the one you never have to modify — write once, clone many.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
A slot is a placeholder inside a shadow tree that marks where content from the light DOM — the element's actual children — should be projected. It is declared with the <slot> element and is the mechanism that makes Web Components composable rather than monolithic.

<template id="card-template">
    <div class="card">
        <header class="card-header">
            <slot name="title">Untitled</slot>
        </header>
        <main class="card-body">
            <slot>No content provided.</slot>
        </main>
    </div>
</template>

<my-card>
    <h2 slot="title">Hello</h2>
    <p>This is the body.</p>
</my-card>

The <slot name="title"> in the shadow tree receives the <h2 slot="title"> from the light DOM. The unnamed <slot> receives the <p>. Neither element is moved, cloned, or duplicated — the light DOM content is projected into the shadow tree for rendering purposes only.

Slots are the answer to a fundamental question in component design: how does a component let consumers inject their own content into a predefined structure?

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Slots serve several essential purposes:

  • Content projection — the core composition mechanism of Web Components.
  • Composition over configuration — consumers use HTML, not props.
  • Reusability — one component template, arbitrary consumer content.
  • Encapsulation with openness — Shadow DOM encapsulates styles; slots admit content.
  • Declarative API — consumers write standard HTML, no JavaScript required.
  • Accessibility preservation — projected content retains its native semantics.
  • Framework parity — the same concept exists as children in React, slots in Vue, ng-content in Angular.
  • Encapsulation integrity — the shadow tree remains isolated; only content flows through explicit openings.

Slots are the difference between a component that is something and a component that contains something.

docs.title: Where It Fits
docs.text:
Web Components
│
├── Templates           ← reusable markup
├── Slots               ← content projection (THIS CHAPTER)
├── Shadow DOM          ← style and structure encapsulation
├── Custom Elements     ← reusable component definitions
└── Declarative Shadow DOM ← server-rendered shadow roots

Slots sit between templates and Shadow DOM. Templates define the shadow structure; slots specify where consumer content enters; Shadow DOM ensures the surrounding implementation remains encapsulated.

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text:
A Web Component with Shadow DOM is encapsulated — its internal structure and styles are isolated from the page. But encapsulation alone produces a closed component: one that renders fixed content and cannot be customized by its consumers.

Consider a component defined like this:

class UserCard extends HTMLElement {
    connectedCallback() {
        this.attachShadow({ mode: 'open' }).innerHTML = `
            <div class="card">
                <h2>User Name</h2>
                <p>User bio here.</p>
            </div>
        `;
    }
}

A consumer using <user-card> has no way to provide the user's name or bio. The component's content is hardcoded. To change it, the consumer would need to:

  • Modify the component's source code.
  • Pass data through attributes or properties and hope the component renders it correctly.
  • Abandon Shadow DOM entirely.

None of these are satisfactory. The component is closed — it does not accept content.

Slots solve this problem. They mark places in the shadow tree where light DOM content should appear:

<my-card>
    <h2 slot="title">Alice</h2>
    <p>Alice is a software engineer.</p>
</my-card>

The component projects the consumer's content into the correct positions. It becomes open — accepting content from its consumers.

docs.title: Previous Limitations
docs.text: Limitation Consequence No content projection Components were monolithic Hardcoded content Consumers could not customize Attribute-only API Complex markup was impossible No style encapsulation Component styles leaked to projected content No composition model Components could not nest cleanly No native HTML mechanism Every framework invented its own

docs.title: Why It Was Introduced
docs.text:
The <slot> element was introduced as part of the Shadow DOM specification (2014–2016). It was designed to solve the composition problem in Web Components.

Before slots, developers used several workarounds:

  • innerHTML passthrough — copy the element's innerHTML into the shadow tree (breaks encapsulation).
  • Template attributes — serialize content into attributes (limited, insecure).
  • No Shadow DOM — accept style leakage in exchange for content flexibility.

Slots formalized content projection as a first-class platform primitive. They shipped alongside Shadow DOM in Chrome 53 (2016), Firefox 63 (2018), Safari 10 (2016), and Edge 79 (2020).

Slots are inspired by similar mechanisms in other platforms:

  • XBL (XUL) — Mozilla's bindings had a similar concept.
  • Flex/Flash — content projection in component frameworks.
  • Frameworks — React children, Vue slots, Angular ng-content.

In 2026, slots are baseline and universally supported. They are the standard mechanism for content projection in Web Components, used by Lit, FAST, Stencil, and every major component library.

docs.title: The Minimal Slot
docs.text:
<!-- Component definition (shadow tree) -->
<template id="wrapper-template">
    <div class="wrapper">
        <slot></slot>
    </div>
</template>

<script>
    class Wrapper extends HTMLElement {
        constructor() {
            super();
            const shadow = this.attachShadow({ mode: 'open' });
            const template = document.getElementById('wrapper-template');
            shadow.appendChild(template.content.cloneNode(true));
        }
    }
    customElements.define('x-wrapper', Wrapper);
</script>

<!-- Component usage (light DOM) -->
<x-wrapper>
    <p>This content is projected into the slot.</p>
</x-wrapper>

docs.title: Code Breakdown
docs.text:
• <slot> — the placeholder inside the shadow tree.
  • The <p> from the light DOM is projected into the slot.
  • The rendered output combines <div class="wrapper"> from the shadow with <p> from the light DOM.

docs.title: Named Slots
docs.text:
<template id="card-template">
    <div class="card">
        <header><slot name="title"></slot></header>
        <main><slot name="body"></slot></main>
        <footer><slot name="footer"></slot></footer>
    </div>
</template>

<my-card>
    <h2 slot="title">Card Title</h2>
    <p slot="body">Card body content.</p>
    <small slot="footer">Footer note.</small>
</my-card>

docs.title: Code Breakdown
docs.text:
• <slot name="title"> — receives content with slot="title".
  • <slot name="body"> — receives content with slot="body".
  • <slot name="footer"> — receives content with slot="footer".
  • The slot attribute on the light DOM elements matches the name on the slot.

docs.title: The Default Slot
docs.text:
<template id="card-template">
    <div class="card">
        <slot name="title"></slot>
        <slot></slot>  <!-- default slot -->
    </div>
</template>

<my-card>
    <h2 slot="title">Card Title</h2>
    <p>This goes into the default slot.</p>
    <p>So does this.</p>
</my-card>

docs.title: Code Breakdown
docs.text:
• The unnamed <slot> is the default slot.
  • Any light DOM content without a slot attribute goes into the default slot.
  • Multiple elements can be projected into the same slot.
  • The order of slotted elements follows their DOM order.

docs.title: Fallback Content
docs.text:
<template id="card-template">
    <div class="card">
        <slot name="title">Untitled</slot>
        <slot>No content provided.</slot>
    </div>
</template>

docs.title: Code Breakdown
docs.text:
• Content inside <slot> is fallback content.
  • It is rendered only when no matching light DOM content is provided.
  • Fallback content is optional — a slot with no fallback renders nothing when empty.

docs.title: Multiple Slots in a Component
docs.text:
<template id="user-card-template">
    <div class="user-card">
        <slot name="avatar"></slot>
        <div class="info">
            <slot name="name"></slot>
            <slot name="email"></slot>
        </div>
        <slot name="actions"></slot>
    </div>
</template>

<user-card>
    <img slot="avatar" src="alice.jpg" alt="Alice">
    <span slot="name">Alice</span>
    <span slot="email">alice@example.com</span>
    <button slot="actions">Follow</button>
</user-card>

docs.title: Code Breakdown
docs.text:
• Four named slots: avatar, name, email, actions.
  • Each slot receives the corresponding light DOM element.
  • Content is projected into the correct position.

docs.title: The slot Attribute
docs.text:
<!-- The slot attribute on the light DOM element matches the name -->
<h2 slot="title">Title</h2>

<!-- Corresponding slot in the shadow tree -->
<slot name="title"></slot>

docs.title: The assignedSlot Property
docs.text:
const h2 = document.querySelector('h2[slot="title"]');
console.log(h2.assignedSlot); // <slot name="title">

docs.title: The slotAssignment Property
docs.text: shadowRoot.slotAssignment; // "named" (default) or "manual"

docs.title: The slotchange Event
docs.text:
const slot = shadowRoot.querySelector('slot');
slot.addEventListener('slotchange', () => {
    console.log('Slot content changed:', slot.assignedNodes());
});

docs.title: Code Breakdown
docs.text:
• slotchange fires when the slot's assigned nodes change.
  • Fires on initial assignment and when content is added or removed.
  • The event is asynchronous — batched to the end of the microtask.

docs.title: The Imperative Slot API
docs.text:
// Requires slotAssignment: "manual"
shadowRoot.slotAssignment = 'manual';
slot.assign(element1, element2);

docs.title: Code Breakdown
docs.text:
• slot.assign(...) — imperatively assigns nodes to a slot.
  • Requires slotAssignment: "manual".
  • Useful for advanced projection scenarios where named assignment is insufficient.

docs.title: The ::slotted() CSS Pseudo-Element
docs.text:
/* Styles slotted content from within the shadow tree */
::slotted(h2) {
    color: blue;
    font-size: 1.5rem;
}

::slotted(p) {
    margin: 0;
}

docs.title: Code Breakdown
docs.text:
• ::slotted() — styles light DOM content from within the shadow tree.
  • Only top-level slotted elements can be styled — descendants cannot.
  • Styles do not leak into slotted content — only the top-level element is targeted.

docs.title: The assignedNodes() and assignedElements() Methods
docs.text:
slot.assignedNodes();              // all assigned nodes (elements + text)
slot.assignedElements();           // only element nodes
slot.assignedNodes({ flatten: true }); // includes fallback content

docs.title: The "Content Projection" Mental Model
docs.text:
Think of slots as windows in the shadow tree through which light DOM content is visible:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  SHADOW DOM (component's internal structure) │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐│
│  │  <div class="card">                     ││
│  │    <header>                             ││
│  │      <slot name="title">  ←── window    ││
│  │    </header>                            ││
│  │    <main>                               ││
│  │      <slot>               ←── window    ││
│  │    </main>                              ││
│  │  </div>                                 ││
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────┘│
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                    ▲
                    │ projects
                    │
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  LIGHT DOM (consumer's content)              │
│  <h2 slot="title">Title</h2>  ───┐          │
│  <p>Body content.</p>  ──────────┘          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Slots are the windows. Light DOM content shows through them.

docs.title: The "Theater Seating" Mental Model
docs.text:
Think of slots as reserved seating:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  THEATER (shadow tree)                       │
│                                              │
│  Row A: [slot name="title"]  ← reserved     │
│  Row B: [slot name="body"]   ← reserved     │
│  Row C: [slot]               ← general      │
│                                              │
│  Attendees (light DOM content)              │
│  ├── <h2 slot="title"> → Row A              │
│  ├── <p slot="body">   → Row B              │
│  └── <p>              → Row C               │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Named slots are reserved seats. The default slot is general admission.

docs.title: The "Named vs Unnamed" Mental Model
docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  NAMED SLOTS                                 │
│  └── <slot name="title">                     │
│  └── Receives content with slot="title"      │
│  └── Multiple named slots per shadow tree    │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  DEFAULT SLOT (unnamed)                      │
│  └── <slot>                                  │
│  └── Receives content with no slot attribute │
│  └── Only one default slot per shadow tree   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Every shadow tree can have multiple named slots but only one default slot.

docs.title: The "Encapsulation with Openings" Mental Model
docs.text:
Shadow DOM provides full encapsulation — styles do not leak in, structure does not leak out. But encapsulation without openings is a monolith. Slots are the openings:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  SHADOW DOM                                  │
│  ├── Styles: encapsulated                    │
│  ├── Structure: encapsulated                 │
│  └── Slots: the only openings                │
│                                              │
│  Light DOM content enters through slots.    │
│  Nothing else crosses the boundary.         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Slots are the API of a component — the only way for consumers to inject content.

docs.title: The "Declarative API" Mental Model
docs.text:
Slots provide a declarative API for component composition:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  ATTRIBUTE API (alternative)                 │
│  <my-card title="Hello" body="World">        │
│  └── Works for simple strings                │
│  └── Cannot accept complex markup            │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  SLOT API (preferred)                        │
│  <my-card>                                   │
│    <h2 slot="title">Hello</h2>               │
│    <p slot="body">World</p>                  │
│  </my-card>                                  │
│  └── Accepts any markup                      │
│  └── Declarative                              │
│  └── Native HTML syntax                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Slots let consumers use native HTML to provide content. No JavaScript needed on the consumer's side.

docs.title: The "Fallback Content" Mental Model
docs.text:
A slot can provide fallback content that renders when no light DOM content is supplied:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  <slot name="title">Untitled</slot>          │
│                                              │
│  If consumer provides <h2 slot="title">      │
│    → "Untitled" is replaced by the <h2>     │
│                                              │
│  If consumer provides nothing                │
│    → "Untitled" is rendered                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Fallback content is the default value for a slot.

docs.title: Concept 1: The <slot> Element
docs.text: A placeholder in the shadow tree that marks where light DOM content should be projected.

docs.title: Concept 2: Named Slots
docs.text:
Slots with a name attribute receive content with a matching slot attribute.

<slot name="title">    ← receives <h2 slot="title">

docs.title: Concept 3: The Default Slot
docs.text: An unnamed <slot> receives all light DOM content without a slot attribute.

docs.title: Concept 4: Fallback Content
docs.text: Content inside <slot> that renders when no matching light DOM content is provided.

docs.title: Concept 5: The slot Attribute
docs.text: The attribute on light DOM elements that assigns them to a named slot.

docs.title: Concept 6: The assignedSlot Property
docs.text: A property on light DOM elements that returns the slot they are assigned to.

docs.title: Concept 7: The assignedNodes() Method
docs.text:
A method on slots that returns the nodes projected into the slot.

slot.assignedNodes(); // the projected nodes
slot.assignedNodes({ flatten: true }); // includes fallback content

docs.title: Concept 8: The assignedElements() Method
docs.text:
A method on slots that returns only the element nodes projected into the slot.

slot.assignedElements(); // element nodes only

docs.title: Concept 9: The slotchange Event
docs.text: An event that fires when a slot's assigned nodes change — on initial assignment and on content changes. It is asynchronous, firing at the end of the current microtask.

docs.title: Concept 10: The ::slotted() Pseudo-Element
docs.text: A CSS pseudo-element that styles slotted content from within the shadow tree. Only top-level slotted elements can be styled.

docs.title: Concept 11: Fallback Content vs. Assigned Content
docs.text:
• Assigned content — light DOM content projected into the slot.
  • Fallback content — the slot's own children, shown only when no assigned content.

docs.title: Concept 12: Multiple Elements in One Slot
docs.text: Multiple light DOM elements can be assigned to the same slot. They are rendered in DOM order.

docs.title: Concept 13: Nested Slots
docs.text:
A slotted element can contain its own shadow DOM with its own slots.

<outer-component>
    <inner-component slot="content">
        <p slot="inner">Nested content</p>
    </inner-component>
</outer-component>

docs.title: Concept 14: Imperative Slot Assignment
docs.text: The slotAssignment: "manual" option allows imperative slot assignment via slot.assign().

docs.title: Concept 15: The slot Attribute Restriction
docs.text:
The slot attribute is only meaningful for direct children of the shadow host. Nested descendants are not assigned.

<my-card>
    <div>
        <h2 slot="title">Nested</h2>  <!-- NOT assigned -->
    </div>
</my-card>

docs.title: Concept 16: Shadow DOM Encapsulation
docs.text: Slots do not break encapsulation. The slotted content is still in the light DOM; the shadow tree only renders it.

docs.title: Concept 17: Style Encapsulation
docs.text: Shadow styles do not apply to slotted content. To style slotted content, use ::slotted().

docs.title: Concept 18: Style Inheritance
docs.text: CSS properties (like color, font-family) inherit through the shadow boundary into slotted content. Only non-inherited properties are encapsulated.

docs.title: Concept 19: Accessibility and Slots
docs.text: Slotted content retains its native semantics. The accessibility tree sees the projected content in its rendered position.

docs.title: Concept 20: Slot Fallback Content Is Optional
docs.text: Fallback content is optional. A slot without fallback content renders nothing when no content is assigned.

docs.title: Step-by-Step: Content Projection
docs.text:
1.  Consumer writes:
    <my-card>
        <h2 slot="title">Hello</h2>
        <p>World</p>
    </my-card>
    │
    ▼
2.  Browser parses the light DOM.
    │   └── <h2> and <p> are children of <my-card>.
    │
    ▼
3.  Custom element's connectedCallback runs.
    │   └── attachShadow() creates a shadow root.
    │
    ▼
4.  Template is cloned into the shadow root.
    │   └── Shadow tree has <slot name="title"> and default <slot>.
    │
    ▼
5.  Browser performs slot assignment.
    │   └── <h2 slot="title"> → slot[name="title"]
    │   └── <p> → default slot
    │
    ▼
6.  Rendered output:
    │   └── Shadow tree structure with projected content.
    │
    ▼
7.  Accessibility tree reflects the rendered output.

docs.title: Step-by-Step: Slot Assignment Algorithm
docs.text:
1.  For each slot in the shadow tree:
    │
    ▼
2.  Find light DOM children of the host with a matching slot attribute:
    │   ├── Named slot: match slot="name"
    │   └── Default slot: match no slot attribute
    │
    ▼
3.  Assign the matched elements to the slot.
    │
    ▼
4.  If no elements are assigned:
    │   └── Render the slot's fallback content.
    │
    ▼
5.  The slot's assigned nodes are rendered in the slot's position.

docs.title: Step-by-Step: The slotchange Event
docs.text:
1.  Slot is created.
    │
    ▼
2.  Content is assigned to the slot.
    │
    ▼
3.  slotchange event fires (initial assignment).
    │
    ▼
4.  Consumer adds/removes content.
    │
    ▼
5.  slotchange event fires again.
    │
    ▼
6.  Listener can react to the change.

docs.title: Step-by-Step: ::slotted() Style Application
docs.text:
1.  Shadow styles include ::slotted(h2) { color: blue; }.
    │
    ▼
2.  Consumer provides <h2 slot="title">.
    │
    ▼
3.  Browser assigns <h2> to slot[name="title"].
    │
    ▼
4.  Shadow styles apply to the top-level slotted element.
    │
    ▼
5.  The <h2> renders in blue.

docs.title: Step-by-Step: The Flattened Tree
docs.text:
1.  Shadow tree is parsed.
    │
    ▼
2.  Light DOM content is parsed.
    │
    ▼
3.  Slot assignment runs.
    │
    ▼
4.  Browser computes the flattened tree:
    │   └── Shadow tree structure with slotted content inserted.
    │
    ▼
5.  Layout uses the flattened tree.
    │
    ▼
6.  Paint uses the flattened tree.
    │
    ▼
7.  Accessibility tree uses the flattened tree.

docs.title: The Slot Assignment Model
docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  SHADOW HOST (e.g., <my-card>)              │
│  ├── Light DOM children (the "flattened tree" source) │
│  │   ├── <h2 slot="title">                  │
│  │   └── <p>                                │
│  └── Shadow root                             │
│      └── Shadow tree                         │
│          ├── <slot name="title">             │
│          └── <slot>                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

The flattened tree is the combination of the shadow tree and the projected light DOM content. It is what is rendered.

docs.title: The Flattened Tree
docs.text:
Shadow tree + Light DOM → Flattened tree → Rendering

The flattened tree is computed at render time. It is not a persistent data structure — it is a view.

docs.title: The Slot Assignment Algorithm
docs.text:
For each slot in the shadow tree:

  1. If slotAssignment is "named" (default):
  2. Find the slot's name.
  3. Find all light DOM children of the host with a matching slot attribute (or no attribute for the default slot).
  4. Assign those elements to the slot.
  5. If slotAssignment is "manual":
  6. Slots are assigned imperatively via slot.assign().
  7. slotchange fires on assignment changes.

docs.title: The assignedNodes() and assignedElements() Methods
docs.text:
• slot.assignedNodes() — returns all assigned nodes (elements + text).
  • slot.assignedElements() — returns only elements.
  • slot.assignedNodes({ flatten: true }) — includes fallback content when no nodes are assigned.

docs.title: The ::slotted() Selector Implementation
docs.text:
::slotted() is a pseudo-element that targets top-level slotted elements. It is:

  • One level deep — it does not match descendants of slotted elements.
  • Shadow-scoped — it does not apply to elements outside the shadow tree.
  • Specificity-aware — it participates in the cascade with the shadow tree's styles.

docs.title: The slot Attribute and Direct Children
docs.text:
Only direct children of the shadow host are assigned to slots. Grandchildren are not:

<my-card>
    <div>
        <h2 slot="title">Nested</h2>  <!-- NOT assigned -->
    </div>
</my-card>

The <h2> is a grandchild, not a direct child. It is not projected.

docs.title: The slotAssignment Modes
docs.text:
Mode Behavior "named" Default. Slots assigned by name matching. "manual" Slots assigned via slot.assign().

Manual assignment is used for advanced scenarios where the component wants full control over which content goes where.

docs.title: The slotchange Event Timing
docs.text:
slotchange fires:

  • After the shadow root is created and initial content is assigned.
  • After any change to the assigned nodes (added/removed).
  • After slot.assign() is called in manual mode.

The event is asynchronous — it fires at the end of the current microtask, allowing batched changes.

docs.title: The Style Encapsulation Exception
docs.text:
While styles are encapsulated, inherited properties cross the shadow boundary:

  • color, font-family, font-size, line-height — inherit.
  • background-color, border — do not inherit.

This is why slotted content often inherits text styling from the host but not box styling.

docs.title: The Slot Assignment Reflection
docs.text:
Light DOM elements are not moved into the shadow tree. They remain in the light DOM. The shadow tree's slots simply render them in place. This is why:

  • document.querySelector can still find slotted elements.
  • The accessibility tree sees them in their light DOM position.
  • Consumer scripts can manipulate them normally.

docs.title: Slot Lifecycle
docs.text:
1.  Shadow root is created.
    │
    ▼
2.  Shadow tree is populated with templates.
    │
    ▼
3.  Slots are created.
    │
    ▼
4.  Slot assignment algorithm runs.
    │
    ▼
5.  Assigned content is projected.
    │
    ▼
6.  slotchange event fires.
    │
    ▼
7.  Consumer modifies content.
    │
    ▼
8.  slotchange event fires again.

docs.title: Component Lifecycle with Slots
docs.text:
1.  Custom element constructed.
    │
    ▼
2.  connectedCallback runs.
    │
    ▼
3.  attachShadow() creates the shadow root.
    │
    ▼
4.  Template content is cloned into the shadow root.
    │
    ▼
5.  Slots are assigned.
    │
    ▼
6.  slotchange fires.
    │
    ▼
7.  Component may react (e.g., apply styles, attach listeners).

docs.title: The slotchange Event Lifecycle
docs.text:
1.  Shadow root created.
    │
    ▼
2.  Initial slot assignment → slotchange fires.
    │
    ▼
3.  Consumer adds a slotted element → slotchange fires.
    │
    ▼
4.  Consumer removes a slotted element → slotchange fires.
    │
    ▼
5.  Component is removed → no more slotchange.

docs.title: Example 1: Basic Slot
docs.text:
<template id="wrapper-template">
    <div class="wrapper">
        <slot></slot>
    </div>
</template>

<script>
    class Wrapper extends HTMLElement {
        constructor() {
            super();
            const shadow = this.attachShadow({ mode: 'open' });
            const template = document.getElementById('wrapper-template');
            shadow.appendChild(template.content.cloneNode(true));
        }
    }
    customElements.define('x-wrapper', Wrapper);
</script>

<x-wrapper>
    <p>Hello from the light DOM!</p>
</x-wrapper>

Code Breakdown:

  • The template has one default slot.
  • The <p> is projected into the slot.
  • The <div class="wrapper"> wraps the projected content.

docs.title: Example 2: Named Slots
docs.text:
<template id="card-template">
    <div class="card">
        <header class="card-header">
            <slot name="title">Untitled</slot>
        </header>
        <main class="card-body">
            <slot>No content.</slot>
        </main>
        <footer class="card-footer">
            <slot name="footer"></slot>
        </footer>
    </div>
</template>

<my-card>
    <h2 slot="title">Card Title</h2>
    <p>Card body content.</p>
    <small slot="footer">Footer note.</small>
</my-card>

Code Breakdown:

  • Three slots: title, default, footer.
  • Each light DOM element is assigned to the correct slot.
  • Fallback content shows when no element is provided.

docs.title: Example 3: Slotted Styling
docs.text:
<template id="card-template">
    <style>
        .card {
            border: 1px solid #ccc;
            border-radius: 8px;
            padding: 1rem;
        }
        ::slotted(h2) {
            margin-top: 0;
            color: #2c3e50;
        }
        ::slotted(p) {
            margin-bottom: 0;
        }
    </style>
    <div class="card">
        <slot name="title"></slot>
        <slot></slot>
    </div>
</template>

Code Breakdown:

  • ::slotted(h2) styles the top-level <h2> slotted into the component.
  • ::slotted(p) styles the top-level <p>.
  • Only the top-level slotted element is styled — descendants are not.

docs.title: Example 4: Slot Change Detection
docs.text:
class LazyLoader extends HTMLElement {
    constructor() {
        super();
        const shadow = this.attachShadow({ mode: 'open' });
        shadow.innerHTML = `<slot></slot>`;

        const slot = shadow.querySelector('slot');
        slot.addEventListener('slotchange', () => {
            const nodes = slot.assignedElements();
            console.log('Slotted content:', nodes);
            // React to slotted content
        });
    }
}
customElements.define('lazy-loader', LazyLoader);

Code Breakdown:

  • slotchange fires when slot content changes.
  • slot.assignedElements() returns the slotted elements.
  • The component can react to the slotted content.

docs.title: Example 5: Nested Slots
docs.text:
<!-- Outer component -->
<template id="outer-template">
    <div class="outer">
        <slot name="content"></slot>
    </div>
</template>

<!-- Inner component -->
<template id="inner-template">
    <div class="inner">
        <slot name="title"></slot>
        <slot></slot>
    </div>
</template>

<!-- Usage -->
<outer-component>
    <inner-component slot="content">
        <h3 slot="title">Nested Title</h3>
        <p>Nested body content.</p>
    </inner-component>
</outer-component>

Code Breakdown:

  • <inner-component slot="content"> is slotted into the outer's content slot.
  • Within inner-component, its own slots receive <h3 slot="title"> and <p>.
  • Slots can nest arbitrarily.

docs.title: Example 6: Slot Fallback Content
docs.text:
<template id="avatar-template">
    <style>
        .avatar {
            width: 40px;
            height: 40px;
            border-radius: 50%;
            background: #ccc;
            display: inline-block;
            overflow: hidden;
        }
        .avatar img {
            width: 100%;
            height: 100%;
            object-fit: cover;
        }
    </style>
    <div class="avatar">
        <slot>
            <!-- Fallback: an icon -->
            <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor">
                <circle cx="12" cy="8" r="4"></circle>
                <path d="M12 14c-4 0-8 2-8 6v2h16v-2c0-4-4-6-8-6z"></path>
            </svg>
        </slot>
    </div>
</template>

<!-- With content -->
<user-avatar>
    <img src="alice.jpg" alt="Alice">
</user-avatar>

<!-- Without content → fallback icon shows -->
<user-avatar></user-avatar>

Code Breakdown:

  • The fallback content is an SVG icon.
  • When the consumer provides an image, the SVG is not rendered.
  • When no image is provided, the SVG renders.

docs.title: Example 7: Multiple Elements in One Slot
docs.text:
<template id="actions-template">
    <div class="actions">
        <slot name="actions"></slot>
    </div>
</template>

<my-actions>
    <button slot="actions">Save</button>
    <button slot="actions">Cancel</button>
    <button slot="actions">Delete</button>
</my-actions>

Code Breakdown:

  • All three buttons have slot="actions".
  • All are assigned to the actions slot.
  • They render in DOM order.

docs.title: Example 8: The assignedNodes() API
docs.text:
const component = document.querySelector('my-card');
const slot = component.shadowRoot.querySelector('slot[name="title"]');

// Get all assigned nodes
console.log(slot.assignedNodes());

// Get only elements
console.log(slot.assignedElements());

// Include fallback content
console.log(slot.assignedNodes({ flatten: true }));

Code Breakdown:

  • assignedNodes() — all assigned nodes (elements + text).
  • assignedElements() — only elements.
  • { flatten: true } — includes fallback content.

docs.title: Example 9: ::slotted() with Descendants
docs.text:
<template id="article-template">
    <style>
        /* Only the top-level slotted element can be styled */
        ::slotted(article) {
            border: 1px solid #ccc;
            padding: 1rem;
        }

        /* This does NOT work — descendants of slotted content cannot be styled */
        ::slotted(article h2) {
            color: red; /* Invalid */
        }

        /* To style descendants, use inherited properties */
        ::slotted(article) {
            color: #333; /* Inherits into descendants */
        }
    </style>
    <slot></slot>
</template>

Code Breakdown:

  • ::slotted(article) styles the top-level slotted <article>.
  • ::slotted(article h2) is invalid — descendant selectors are not allowed.
  • Only inherited properties (color, font-family) propagate into descendants.

docs.title: Example 10: Complete Card Component with Slots
docs.text:
<template id="product-card-template">
    <style>
        .card {
            display: grid;
            grid-template-areas:
                "image info"
                "actions actions";
            grid-template-columns: 120px 1fr;
            gap: 1rem;
            border: 1px solid #e0e0e0;
            border-radius: 8px;
            padding: 1rem;
            font-family: system-ui, sans-serif;
        }
        .image { grid-area: image; }
        .info { grid-area: info; }
        .actions {
            grid-area: actions;
            display: flex;
            gap: 0.5rem;
        }
        ::slotted(img) {
            width: 120px;
            height: 120px;
            object-fit: cover;
            border-radius: 4px;
        }
        ::slotted(h3) {
            margin: 0 0 0.5rem 0;
            color: #333;
        }
        ::slotted(.price) {
            font-weight: bold;
            color: #2c7a2c;
        }
    </style>
    <div class="card">
        <div class="image"><slot name="image"></slot></div>
        <div class="info">
            <slot name="title"></slot>
            <slot name="price"></slot>
            <slot></slot>
        </div>
        <div class="actions"><slot name="actions"></slot></div>
    </div>
</template>

<script>
    class ProductCard extends HTMLElement {
        constructor() {
            super();
            const shadow = this.attachShadow({ mode: 'open' });
            const template = document.getElementById('product-card-template');
            shadow.appendChild(template.content.cloneNode(true));
        }
    }
    customElements.define('product-card', ProductCard);
</script>

<product-card>
    <img slot="image" src="product.jpg" alt="Product">
    <h3 slot="title">Awesome Product</h3>
    <span slot="price" class="price">$29.99</span>
    <p>This product is amazing.</p>
    <button slot="actions">Buy</button>
    <button slot="actions">Details</button>
</product-card>

Code Breakdown:

  • Four named slots: image, title, price, actions, plus the default slot.
  • Each slot receives the corresponding light DOM element.
  • ::slotted() styles the top-level slotted elements.
  • The component provides a complete layout with flexible content.

docs.title: 10. Common Use Cases
docs.text: Use Case Slot Pattern Card component title, body, footer slots Layout component Default slot for content Tabs tab and panel slots Modals title, body, actions slots Tooltips Default slot for content Accordions header and content slots Lists Default slot for items Dropdowns trigger and menu slots Navigation Default slot for links Data tables header and row slots Avatars Default slot for image Buttons Default slot for text

docs.title: 11. Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use named slots for structured content. Why: clearer API for consumers.
  2. Use the default slot for simple content. Why: simpler for single-content components.
  3. Provide fallback content. Why: renders when no content is provided.
  4. Style slotted content with ::slotted(). Why: shadow styles do not apply to slotted content otherwise.
  5. Only style top-level slotted elements. Why: ::slotted() does not match descendants.
  6. Use inherited properties for deep styling. Why: color and font-family inherit into descendants.
  7. Listen to slotchange to react to content. Why: slotted content may change dynamically.
  8. Use assignedElements() to get slotted elements. Why: filters out text nodes.
  9. Remember that only direct children are slotted. Why: grandchildren are not assigned.
  10. Use slotAssignment: "manual" only when needed. Why: named assignment is the default.
  11. Test slots with dynamic content. Why: slotted content may change at runtime.
  12. Document the slot API. Why: consumers need to know the slot names.
  13. Use consistent slot naming. Why: predictability aids adoption.
  14. Avoid hardcoded content in shadow trees. Why: use slots for flexibility.
  15. Combine slots with Custom Elements. Why: the full Web Components API.
  16. Test on multiple browsers. Why: minor differences in slotchange timing exist.
  17. Use ::slotted() with specific selectors. Why: broad selectors may cause unintended styling.
  18. Consider accessibility. Why: slotted content retains its semantics.
  19. Do not rely on slot order for behavior. Why: order is DOM-based, not slot-based.
  20. Use slots for composition, not for state. Why: slots are for structure.
  21. Document slot fallback behavior. Why: consumers need to know what happens when no content is provided.
  22. Test slotted content with screen readers. Why: verify the accessibility tree is correct.
  23. Use slots with Declarative Shadow DOM. Why: server-rendered shadow DOM uses the same model.
  24. Cache slot references. Why: querying shadow roots is not free.
  25. Audit slots after component changes. Why: API changes affect consumers.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Styling Slotted Content Without ::slotted()
docs.text:
/* Shadow style — does NOT apply to slotted content */
h2 {
    color: blue;
}

Why it's wrong: Shadow styles are encapsulated. They do not apply to slotted content.

✅ Correct:

::slotted(h2) {
    color: blue;
}

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Using Descendant Selectors in ::slotted()
docs.text:
::slotted(article h2) {
    color: red; /* Invalid */
}

Why it's wrong: ::slotted() only matches top-level slotted elements. Descendant selectors are not allowed.

✅ Correct:

::slotted(article) {
    color: #333; /* Inherits into descendants */
}

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Expecting Grandchildren to Be Slotted
docs.text:
<my-card>
    <div>
        <h2 slot="title">Title</h2>  <!-- NOT slotted -->
    </div>
</my-card>

Why it's wrong: Only direct children of the shadow host are assigned to slots.

✅ Correct:

<my-card>
    <h2 slot="title">Title</h2>  <!-- Direct child — slotted -->
</my-card>

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Not Providing Fallback Content
docs.text:
<slot name="title"></slot>

Why it's wrong: When no content is provided, the slot renders nothing.

✅ Correct:

<slot name="title">Untitled</slot>

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Using the Wrong Slot Name
docs.text:
<!-- Component definition -->
<slot name="heading"></slot>

<!-- Consumer -->
<h2 slot="title">Title</h2>  <!-- Wrong name -->

Why it's wrong: The slot names do not match. The content is not projected.

✅ Correct:

<h2 slot="heading">Title</h2>

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Relying on Slot Order
docs.text:
<slot name="first"></slot>
<slot name="second"></slot>

Why it's wrong: Consumers may provide content in any order. Slot order is determined by the shadow tree, not by the consumer's markup.

✅ Correct: Do not rely on slot order for behavior — use named slots with a clear contract.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Forgetting slotchange Fires Asynchronously
docs.text:
slot.addEventListener('slotchange', () => {
    // This runs at the end of the microtask, not immediately
});

Why it's wrong: If you need synchronous access, you may be surprised.

✅ Correct: Understand the async nature of slotchange.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Mutating Slotted Content Directly
docs.text:
slot.assignedElements().forEach(el => el.remove());

Why it's wrong: Removes the consumer's content — they own it, not the component.

✅ Correct: Do not remove consumer content. Use slotchange to react, not to mutate.

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Using assignedNodes() When assignedElements() Is Better
docs.text:
const nodes = slot.assignedNodes();
// nodes may include text nodes

Why it's wrong: Text nodes may be present (whitespace). Use assignedElements() for elements only.

✅ Correct:

const elements = slot.assignedElements();

docs.title: ❌ Mistake: Not Testing Slots with Dynamic Content
docs.text:
Why it's wrong: Consumers may add/remove content at runtime. slotchange handles this, but it must be tested.

✅ Correct: Test with dynamic content insertion and removal.

docs.title: 13. Performance Considerations
docs.text:
• Slot assignment is fast — linear in the number of slotted elements.
  • slotchange fires asynchronously — batched at the microtask level.
  • ::slotted() selectors are efficient — only match top-level slotted elements.
  • Shadow DOM styles are scoped — style recalculation is faster.
  • Slots do not clone content — they project it. No duplication.
  • Slotted content retains its identity — no wrapper elements.

docs.title: Performance Tips
docs.text:
1. Use slots instead of cloning content into the shadow tree.
  2. Minimize slotchange listeners.
  3. Cache slot references.
  4. Use assignedElements() over assignedNodes().
  5. Batch DOM changes.
  6. Avoid deeply nested slot structures.

docs.title: Slotted Content Is Trusted
docs.text: Slotted content comes from the consumer. The component cannot sanitize it — the consumer is responsible.

docs.title: Slot Injection
docs.text: If a component injects consumer content into innerHTML, XSS is possible. Use textContent or sanitize.

docs.title: Shadow DOM Isolation
docs.text: Shadow DOM does not prevent XSS. Scripts inside slotted content still run in the document context.

docs.title: Slots and CSP
docs.text: Slots do not affect CSP. Slotted scripts are still subject to CSP.

docs.title: Slot Names and DOM Clobbering
docs.text: Slot names should not conflict with global identifiers. Use clear, specific names.

docs.title: ::slotted() and CSS Injection
docs.text: ::slotted() is safe — it does not allow arbitrary CSS injection.

docs.title: Fallback Content and Trust
docs.text: Fallback content is defined by the component, not the consumer. It is trusted. Do not inject user-controlled content into fallback content.

docs.title: 15. Debugging Tips
docs.text:
• Chrome DevTools → Elements — inspect shadow trees and slots.
  • Chrome DevTools → Elements → Shadow tree — expand the shadow root.
  • $0.shadowRoot — the shadow root of the selected element.
  • $0.shadowRoot.querySelector('slot') — the slots in the shadow tree.
  • $0.shadowRoot.querySelector('slot').assignedElements() — the slotted elements.
  • $0.assignedSlot — the slot the element is assigned to.
  • slot.assignedNodes() — all assigned nodes.
  • slot.assignedElements() — elements only.
  • slotchange event — inspect slotted content changes.
  • DevTools → Accessibility — inspect the accessibility tree with slotted content.
  • getComputedStyle(slottedElement) — inspect styles applied via ::slotted().
  • Test with dynamic content — add/remove slotted content at runtime.
  • Test with no content — verify fallback content renders.
  • Test with extra content — verify unassigned content is handled.

docs.title: 16. When to Use
docs.text:
• Composable components — cards, modals, tabs, layouts.
  • Content projection — accept content from consumers.
  • Fallback content — provide defaults.
  • Declarative APIs — let consumers use HTML.
  • Layout components — wrappers, containers.
  • Web Components — every component with consumer content.
  • Design systems — flexible, composable components.

docs.title: 17. When Not to Use
docs.text:
• Do not use slots for state. Use properties or attributes.
  • Do not use slots for simple strings. Use attributes or properties.
  • Do not use slots for events. Use custom events.
  • Do not use slots when content is fixed. Hardcode markup instead.
  • Do not use slots to sanitize content. Slotted content is the consumer's responsibility.
  • Do not rely on slot order for behavior. Use named slots.
  • Do not style descendants of slotted content directly. Use ::slotted() on top-level elements or inherited properties.

  • slot attribute
